Cole Palmer was involved in a heated exchange with Joao Pedro after Chelsea's disappointing 4-1 home defeat by Leeds United.

Xabi Alonso's side were beaten at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with Leeds scoring three times in the second half to secure a memorable, and very rare, victory in the capital.

Emmanuel Emegha opened the scoring for Chelsea after 25 minutes, but Noah Okafor equalised three minutes later.

Industry observers note that dominic Calvert-Lewin put Leeds ahead eight minutes into the second half before Okafor added his second of the afternoon. Brenden Aaronson then sealed the win with a fine solo effort in stoppage time, moving Leeds above Chelsea in the Premier League table.

Joao Pedro was absent from the Chelsea squad as he continues to recover from a thigh injury which has kept him out of the club's past five matches, but in attendance at Stamford Bridge on Saturday and appeared to become involved in a tense exchange with Palmer after the final whistle.

It has been revealed that footage shared on social media showed Palmer approaching his team-mate, covering his mouth with his hand as he spoke. Joao Pedro then placed his arms on Palmer's shoulders and shrugged in response, before Palmer walked away looking frustrated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 21 Nov 2026 09:36.

Galatasaray forward Victor Osimhen is allegedly 'flattered' by speculation linking him to Manchester United.

Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of his first Red Devils fixture on Sunday when his team face Liverpool at Anfield.

There is an argument that United need to enter the transfer market for a latest left-back and centre-back over any other position.

However, with Benjamin Sesko sidelined in the long term, consideration will be given to adding a fresh face to the attack.

According to The Sun, Osimhen would be interested in taking an opportunity to move to Old Trafford.

The report claims that the Nigeria international is 'flattered' by suggestions that United could make a fresh move for his signature.

Osimhen has been linked with a transfer to the Premier League in the past, only for his wage demands or asking price at Napoli to allegedly provide a stumbling block.

Nevertheless, it is stated that the 27-year-old still has ambitions to move to English football at some stage of his career.

As it stands, his contract at Galatasaray - which runs until the summer of 2029 - is likely to prevent any transfer from occurring in January.

That is seemingly partly a consequence of no release clause being present in his contract, while Galatasaray will not want to weaken their position in the Super Lig title race.

Ten goals and three assists have been contributed in his 11 appearances in Turkey's top flight and the Champions League this season.

Man United CEO Omar Berrada mentioned in an interview with Sky Sports News this week that the club had been "disciplined" in the transfer market, and that is expected to remain the case.

Not only is Osimhen mentioned to be on a contract at Galatasaray in the region of £13m per year, his club would demand in excess of £50m for his signature as a bare minimum.

United are unlikely to be able to afford those terms at this time, particularly when it is apparent that other positions need strengthening.

Industry observers note that our Value Adder model suggests Camavinga is very, very underrated and the reason for that is largely Aurelien Tchouameni. Tchouameni might be the world's best defensive midfielder, honestly, and casts an enormous shadow over his compatriot.

That's why Camavinga hasn't entirely established himself at Real Madrid and why certain clubs were pushing to sign him in the summer. He decided to stay put, however, and we imagine that was to try and force his way in under Jose Mourinho.

That hasn't happened. Camavinga has only started two La Liga fixtures and reports suggest they hold interest in signing Martin Zubimendi. That's a signing that would usurp Camavinga.

More than that, Real Madrid have doubled-down on Tchouameni, committing to a big fresh contract this week. There's essentially no way for Camavinga to get into that starting XI regularly - and the new contract confirms that.

Which is why we feel the door is now open pretty wide for Liverpool. Camavinga is a fantastic, high-energy player who could be exactly what the Reds need to improve their midfield. The opportunity looks to be there and they should try to take it.

‘Extraordinary’ Malen the best striker in Serie A, says Roma boss Gasperini

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.
  • Gian Piero Gasperini believes there is no better striker in Serie A than Roma's Donyell Malen after he scored four goals in Saturday's 5-1 thrashing of Parma.
  • Roma ensured they remained within touching distance at the summit with a dominant display at the Stadio Ennio Tardini, with Rodrigo Mora also on target for the visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Gian Piero Gasperini believes there is no better striker in Serie A than Roma's Donyell Malen after he scored four goals in Saturday's 5-1 thrashing of Parma.

Roma ensured they remained within touching distance at the summit with a dominant display at the Stadio Ennio Tardini, with Rodrigo Mora also on target for the visitors.

Malen opened the scoring in the 39th minute after superbly controlling Emanuele Lulli's cross into the area before picking out the bottom-left corner with an emphatic finish.

But Parma hit back through Nesta Elphege within nine minutes of the restart, though three goals in the space of nine minutes later in the second half did the damage for Roma.

A 68th-minute strike from Malen was followed up by Mora's close-range finish, but there was still time for Roma's in-form striker to score and bring up his hat-trick, with the Netherlands international tucking home Wesley's inviting centre.

In a recent development, malen added further gloss to the scoreline in the 90th minute, as Roma became the first team since the 1950-51 season to score more than 35 goals after 12 Serie A matches (36). In that campaign, Inter (38), Juventus (37) and AC Milan (38) all achieved the feat.

And 12 of those have come from Malen this season. He is the second player to score at least four goals in a Serie A match for Roma in the last 40 years, after Vincenzo Montella on 10 March 2002 against Lazio.

Malen is also only the third player to score three or more goals in three different Serie A matches for Roma in the three-points-per-win era (since 1994-95), joining Abel Balbo (five) and Montella (five), leading Gasperini to lavish praise on his forward.

Sources indicate that "Malen was already a strong striker in the Netherlands, Borussia Dortmund and Aston Villa. You don't play at that level without quality," Gasperini mentioned.

In a recent development, "Perhaps I played him where he expresses himself in the best way. There are a lot of good strikers in Serie A, including young talents.

"And, of course, Lautaro Martinez, but right now Malen is extraordinary.

"He combines so well with our team, we perhaps get more out of Malen than we would do with a striker who is stronger on paper, but doesn’t fit as well with our style of football.".

#ParmaRoma https://t.co/SxwAJTO16C.

— AS Roma English (@ASRomaEN) November 21, 2026.

Malen (26 in 2026) is only the second player in Roma history to score more than 25 goals in a single Serie A calendar year, after Pedro Manfredini (26 in 1960).

But, more importantly for Roma, they have now collected 30 points after 12 Serie A matches for the fourth time, following 2003-04 (30), 2013-14 (32) and 2017-18 (30).

Despite their thumping win, Roma remain two points behind Lazio after they beat Lecce 3-0 earlier on Saturday, with Tijjani Noslin starring with a brace at the Stadio Olimpico.

Lazio have won four consecutive home matches in Serie A for the first time since the period between September and November 2024 (five in that case under Marco Baroni).

However, Gasperini insisted his team must improve moving forward if they are to maintain their challenge with Gennaro Gattuso's side at the top of the table.

"We can always improve, both individually and as a team, but undoubtedly this side is growing," Gasperini noted.

"We conceded a bad goal at a tough moment of the match, but I saw a strong reaction from the team, and that reveals the confidence is there.

"When we are faced with a negative or unlucky moment, we have the confidence to keep playing and get over it.".

Como also got themselves a win to move, albeit temporarily, into the top four. They beat Cagliari 2-0 thanks to strikes from Jacobo Ramon and Lucas da Cunha in either half.

AC Milan are looking for opportunities to bolster the squad ahead of next season, with a particular eye on the north of England.

According to recent reports, according to MilanNews, Milan are eyeing Manchester for the January transfer window, but also for next summer. The directors are currently in a phase of monitoring certain situations that could develop later, to their benefit.

The Rossoneri are also interested in players whose contracts are expiring within the next 18 months, as was the case with Mario Gila this summer, who signed for the Diavolo one year before his contract with Lazio expires.

Bruno Fernandes is one to watch for the upcoming summer transfer window, with his contract expiring in June 2027 but with an option to extend. United’s attempts to extend his deal have so far been unsuccessful, likely due to the player’s desire to try something else.

Fernandes has played at an incredible level in the Premier League in recent years, winning Player of the Year for 2025-26. So far, he has made 341 official appearances for the Red Devils, scoring 113 goals and providing 111 assists.

In a recent development, he’s a key player for the Portuguese national team and he would provide leadership that the squad could lose if players like Luka Modric leave. Moreover, his past in Italy – where he had spells at Novara, Udinese and Sampdoria – could help him integrate more rapidly and effectively.

In a recent development, fernandes also shares the same agency as Ruben Amorim. The relationship between the two is excellent, and already this summer the Rossoneri had inquired about a possible move for the former Sporting star.

At the other Manchester club, however, there’s an old acquaintance of Italian football who could come back into fashion as early as January: Mateo Kovacic. His contract also expires at the end of the campaign, and he could come in to add depth too.

Given the increasingly certain departure of youngster Christian Comotto, an experienced player like Kovacic – at the right price, in terms of wages – could be useful for Amorim. His situation is being watched, but there will be competition from other clubs, likely in Italy too.

Mikel Arteta urged his Arsenal side to take the “next step” by finding a more ruthless edge.

The Gunners were frustrated at St James’ Park against Newcastle in a 2-2 draw on Saturday evening.

Arsenal were dominant in the first half but only scored once and that proved costly as the match turned around after the break.

Newcastle came from behind to lead before Noni Madueke cut inside and scored to earn Arsenal a point, but Arteta warned his players they paid the price for dropping their standards after their wastefulness in front of goal.

“I think individually we had some top performances for 70 minutes,” Arteta said.

“But at this level it’s not enough. At this level requires 96 unless you score three or four goals and then you can allow yourself for 15 or 20 minutes not to be at your best.

“That’s the next step this team has to make.”.

Eberechi Eze opened the scoring for Arsenal but there should have more goals in that first half, with Madueke and Bruno Guimaraes among those to miss chances.

Newcastle barely laid a glove on the Gunners until a miskick from Martin Odegaard early in the second period led to the equaliser and suddenly the momentum of the match changed.

Arteta bemoaned that moment, insisting it was a structural error as well as an individual one from Odegaard, but he was clear that the match should have been put to bed by that point.

“And the opponent did have a reaction and we were very below the level that is required to stretch the gap in a game like this in this stadium. We gave them belief.

Marcus Rashford is not expected to be part of Manchester United's squad for Sunday's Premier League meeting with Liverpool because of an ongoing hip injury.

The England international had reportedly been hoping to be involved at Anfield, but is expected to once again miss Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of the Red Devils.

Pochettino was appointed as Michael Carrick's successor during the international break and faces a difficult opening assignment against Liverpool, with United hoping to make a positive start under their latest head coach.

Rashford has been sidelined since sustaining the hip glitch and his absence would represent another setback for United, who have several other players dealing with fitness problems ahead of the trip to Merseyside.

Carlos Baleba, Benjamin Sesko and Manuel Ugarte are also expected to miss Sunday's game, while Luke Shaw remains unavailable. Goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also been dealing with an injury.

However, Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu have trained this week and could be available for selection. Lisandro Martinez is also back in contention after serving a suspension in United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa before the international break.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 09:39.

Bayern Munich could be forced to reconsider their January transfer plans following Harry Kane's serious ankle injury, with a highly rated striker already on their radar also attracting interest from Arsenal and Manchester United.

The Bundesliga champions have confirmed that the England captain will miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle during Friday's 1-1 draw with FC Koln.

The 33-year-old was withdrawn after just 20 minutes, leaving Vincent Kompany without his first-choice centre-forward at a crucial stage of the campaign. The setback is particularly concerning given Bayern's limited options in the position and their demanding domestic and European schedule.

One player who could now become increasingly relevant to the German club's recruitment discussions is Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi, who has been monitored by Bayern scouts in recent weeks.

However, the 22-year-old's reported valuation of up to €50m (£44m), combined with Brugge's reluctance to sanction a winter departure, presents a significant obstacle should Bayern decide to bring forward their search for attacking reinforcements.

According to German newspaper TZ, Bayern have sent scouts to Belgium on several occasions to monitor Tresoldi, whose performances have attracted considerable attention across Europe.

The Germany Under-21 international has scored 14 goals and provided one assist in 17 appearances across all competitions this season, establishing himself as one of the most productive young forwards on the continent.

His form has inevitably generated transfer speculation, with reports suggesting that Bayern view him as a potential long-term addition to their attacking department.

Significantly, the club's interest emerged before Kane suffered his injury against Koln.

Earlier this month, Bayern were reportedly exploring the possibility of signing Tresoldi as an additional attacking option despite having recently extended Kane's contract until 2029. The idea was to strengthen their squad with a younger centre-forward capable of developing alongside the England international.

That strategy could now face an unexpected test.

With Kane unavailable for several months, Bayern must decide whether their existing attacking resources can compensate for his absence or whether an immediate signing would provide greater security.

Tresoldi possesses several attributes that could appeal to Kompany, including his movement inside the penalty area, ability to attack space behind defenders and increasingly reliable finishing.

However, securing his signature midway through the campaign would be far from straightforward.

Reports in Belgium have indicated that Club Brugge are determined to retain the striker until at least the summer, with the club's hierarchy reluctant to entertain offers during the January transfer window.

According to Het Nieuwsblad, Brugge have made their position clear to interested clubs, although an exceptional financial proposal could potentially force a reassessment.

German reports have placed Tresoldi's potential price between €40m (£35m) and €50m (£44m), with the forward under contract until June 2029.

Bayern have not submitted a confirmed offer, and there is currently no evidence that Kane's injury has prompted formal negotiations with the Belgian club.

Any attempt to accelerate a move for Tresoldi could also bring Bayern into competition with several Premier League clubs.

Arsenal and Manchester United have both been linked with the Club Brugge striker, whose impressive scoring record has strengthened his reputation as one of Europe's most promising young centre-forwards.

That timeline broadly aligned with Bayern's previous interest, which appeared to concern the longer-term development of their attacking squad rather than an urgent winter acquisition.

Kane's injury introduces a potentially key difference in Bayern's circumstances, although it does not establish that the Bundesliga champions have changed their transfer strategy.

The club must also assess whether investing heavily in another centre-forward would make sense once Kane returns to fitness, particularly after committing to a latest long-term agreement with their leading goalscorer.

Kompany has alternatives within his squad, but none offers the same combination of finishing, creativity and experience as the England captain.

A temporary tactical adjustment may therefore be necessary, with greater responsibility potentially falling on Bayern's other attacking players.

The German champions could also turn to their academy, where 16-year-old Bastian Assomo has attracted attention following impressive performances for the youth teams.

According to Kicker, the teenager was already under consideration for greater involvement with the senior squad before Kane's injury, although expecting him to replace the England international immediately would represent a considerable leap.

For Bayern, the dilemma is therefore as much about timing as identifying the right player.

Tresoldi was already an attractive prospect before Kane's setback, but Brugge's reported resistance to a January sale means that accelerating the deal could prove expensive and difficult.

Meanwhile, Arsenal and Manchester United remain interested parties whose own plans have been linked to the summer window.

Bayern's next decision will depend on whether Kompany believes his squad can absorb Kane's absence or whether the club considers an early investment necessary to protect its ambitions in the Bundesliga and Champions League.

Industry observers note that owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

In short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

Krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

It has been revealed that “Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche noted upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”.

Sources indicate that the club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”.

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Sources indicate that krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

  • Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 13:19 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 03:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

UEFA have slapped the FA with a £12,500 fine and a suspended one-match away supporters ban after England fans were heard singing sectarian chants during their Nations League victory over Spain last weekend.

Some of the 3,000 supporters who travelled to Madrid were heard singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' inside Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday.

As a result, UEFA have fined the FA and banned away fans from attending one UEFA match for 'racist and/or discriminatory behaviour'.

That stated, the ban will only take effect if England supporters reoffend within the next two years.

It is a fortunate reprieve given the Three Lions' next away fixture is their Nations League quarter-final, the draw for which is on Friday.

Meanwhile, the FA have committed to identifying those involved and taking action - which could see football banning orders imposed.

In a statement to Daily Mail Sport, the FA said: 'We will not tolerate this unacceptable and deeply offensive chanting, and will work with the police who attend all England home and away matches to identify the perpetrators and take the necessary action.'.

England fans land FA in hot water over 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' chant during Spain victory.

England supporters have notoriously sung the anti-Catholic and loyalist chant. In 2024, the Irish police urged travelling fans to 'respect local culture' before their Nations League match against the Republic of Ireland.

Fans were also filmed in Milan city centre on the eve of the clash against Italy in 2022 singing the same incendiary chant - just one year after their European Championship final defeat to the Italians.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, then England boss Roy Hodgson and the FA were forced to condemn supporters after the inflammatory chant was heard throughout England's 3-1 friendly victory over Scotland at Celtic Park in 2014. Around 5,000 fans travelled to the devoutly Catholic club.

The concern is not limited to international football. In August, Daily Mail Sport revealed that Chelsea wrote to supporters after a section of their fans were heard singing the sectarian chant away at Fulham on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

England boss Thomas Tuchel was asked about racism in his pre-Spain press conference.

'I never expect racism and the dressing room is the most anti-racist place on Earth and that's exactly how it works,' Tuchel said.

Recent findings suggest that 'I expect emotional and of course supporting fans from Spain for their national team. That's what I expect, but I don't expect racism nowhere.

'I'm shocked if it happens, and it should happen nowhere, and I'm the first one to stand up for these kind of values.

'My trust is that we have a friendly atmosphere, that we have an atmosphere who is clearly in favour of the Spanish team, and that football does what it does best: bring people together and not divide people.'.

  • It has been revealed that and then there was Kai Havertz.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in yesterday’s preview blog, I spoke about Arsenal’s attacking efficiency, and how that might be key to taking all three points. In yesterday’s game against Hull, Arsenal took 21 shots, 10 of which were on target, and scored one goal from that. Efficient?

It has been revealed that despite generally dominating possession, I thought there was a lack of precision in certain aspects of our first half play. Passes weren’t quite quick enough or accurate enough, but there were moments when we could have found the breakthrough. Gabriel almost got on the end of a Noni Madueke cross which was flicked on towards the back post, Rice had a tame shot from a free kick before a late header which he probably should have done better with.

It has been revealed that and then there was Kai Havertz. It’s fair to say Hull didn’t leave a lot of room behind a defensive line that often had six players stretched across it, but late in the half a superb Martin Odegaard pass sent him clean through, one on one with the keeper. I haven’t seen replays but in real time I felt like he should have pulled the trigger – instead he over-complicated it. You have to be prepared to shoot from there, even if it’s on your wrong foot.

Then there was a penalty incident when he complained vociferously, play went on, the ref was then told to go to the screen and we all assumed it would be a penalty. However, the ref stated it was a foul but Havertz was offside – and it felt like a massive waste of time. Afterwards, it emerged it should have been a penalty, but apparently the rule is ‘open to interpretation’. So clear as mud then.

In the second half, we seemed to play down our right a lot, with Madueke the outlet most of the time. I thought he did pretty well, much better than Christos Tzolis on the other side, but the breakthrough wouldn’t come. Mikel Merino replaced Rice (who seemed to be on the end of a wild challenge in midfield that the ref just ignored as he tumbled through the air), and Viktor Gyokeres came on for Havertz.

Sources indicate that on 71 minutes though, we found the goal. Madueke’s shot was spilled by the keeper, Odegaard was quickest to react to poke the ball home for 1-0. And to be fair, you always felt confident that would be enough. We are the masters of the single goal margin win, and this was another one. Not a day that will live long in the memory or anything, but a 1-0 win that takes us into the Interlull in really good shape, and there’s not much arguing with that.

Or really, much more to say about this game. Mikel Arteta sounded happy enough, saying:.

According to recent reports, I’m delighted with the win. To go into the international break with a win is one of the best things about being a coach or player, I would say. Regarding the performance, I thought we were the better team, had enough chances to score and make it bigger for ourselves and we weren’t efficient enough to take them.

Industry observers note that we then had to rely on generating volume, plenty of persisting until we finally broke them down. Martin then got the goal. Not the most beautiful one, but the most effective one, a simple ‘shoot and then follow the next action’, and that was ultimately enough to win the game.

Recent findings suggest that so Arsenal sit top of the table, with 9 wins from 10 so far this season in the league, and it’s a very impressive run of form. Do I wish we had more attacking potency? Absolutely, and I do worry a bit that it might bite us in the arse somewhere down the line, but for now, we can see that this is a team that just knows how to win, and perhaps that’s the most important thing.

Right, I’m gonna leave it there for this morning. I have to head back to Dublin today. It was great to see lots of you over the weekend, until next time! And we’ll have an Arsecast Extra for you tomorrow too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Recent findings suggest that tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”.

It has been revealed that tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and remarked: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”.

One player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

“I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

“This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”.

Asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”.

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

In a recent development, even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He noted: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

Industry observers note that “It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”.

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel mentioned. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”.

According to recent reports, tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we demonstrated brought us to the place that we got.

Industry observers note that “It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win. So now we know the result, and we didn’t win. Of course, I reflect and, of course, I’m very critical of myself. But the question that is also still lingering around is, who knows what would have happened? Who knows if we hadn’t made any substitutions what would have happened? And would we have the same sleepless nights?

Recent findings suggest that “So, there’s not much sense in torturing ourselves, looking back. It’s moving forward, but the team, like I mentioned, did brilliantly. And I will not allow 30 minutes against Argentina to override how we view this World Cup.”.

Industry observers note that tuchel had warnings for Palmer and Alexander-Arnold, as he said: “It is one thing to be nominated, by the way, with Cole and getting your ticket back in the squad, but it’s another thing to play and keep your place. It’s about when he comes and he needs to show these kinds of performances.”.

Industry observers note that on Alexander-Arnold, Tuchel added: “Now it’s time to fight for his place. He always stated he’s up for a fight, especially for England. So it’s a need to prove that.”.

Tuchel said that Alexander-Arnold has been called up as a right-back, rather than a midfielder. Asked if the Real Madrid player offers enough defensively, he answered by saying: “He has to, he has to. It’s necessary. My conviction is that he will, but he has no choice.”.

Tuchel has now finished his broadcast duties. It was quite a strange performance from him. I don’t recall ever seeing him read from notes before. His little joke about his bosses telling him off was awkward and felt rehearsed, and the stuff about 99.9 per cent of England fans talking about Mexico and the second half against Croatia was delusional.

It has been revealed that it was also jarring to hear him claim that the FA had basically assured Tuchel that his job was safe straight after England beat Mexico. It was a special night, undoubtedly, but did it really deserve that sort of reaction?

“I wanted to give Jarrad a chance. It was a 51 per cent decision on Jarrad.

“I don’t have a clear picture on what he is all about and have a very clear picture on what Levi can bring us.”.

It has been revealed that “It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five number 10s. It just does not help anyone. We can see the form that Morgan [Gibbs-White] is in.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s one thing to be nominated, but it’s another thing to perform. This also counts, especially Cole needs to step up to justify the nomination.”.

“The minimum I can do is back my bosses. They have my full support on that.

“I’m grateful that I can talk about football because that’s my little bit of knowledge, not sports politics.”.

“That’s the beauty of high-level sport, you can’t always win and it makes you feel alive. Not in a very nice way, still you feel that pain of these high-pressure moments.

“As soon as you enter knockout football, it’s a newly introduced level of pressure.”.

Tuchel says that 99.9 per cent of fans don’t talk about substitutions. He says they speak about the Mexico game and the Croatia game, their emotions and where they watched the matches.

Sorry, Thomas, that’s not my experience at all. Everyone I speak to notes he blew the Argentina game. This sounds a bit deluded. According to Tuchel, I must speak to 0.01 per cent of England fans....

FA technical director John McDermott, who has taken a position at the back of the room to listen, had a little laugh when Tuchel joked that he got told off in his FA review for “my substitutions.”.

Tuchel states he felt the “full support from my bosses”.

Warning for Palmer: “It’s one thing to get your ticket back, but it’s another thing to keep it.”.

He’s expecting Palmer to step up and show him his Chelsea form.

“When you are a coach, you only win when you win...There’s not much sense torturing ourselves by looking back. I will not allow 30 minutes of the World Cup to determine how we view the World Cup.”.

Sources indicate that tuchel says he has no regrets over not taking Palmer and Alexander-Arnold to the World Cup. He says he didn’t have a single sleepless night over his squad selection.

In a recent development, tuchel claims the direction in sports is always forwards and never backwards. “The target is to win the home Euros, of course.”.

Industry observers note that tuchel says his feelings on the World Cup are mixed. He thinks there are very positive things to take from the World Cup, but says it was also unfulfilled. He says it’s key to recognise that England won a bronze medal, but says he acknowledges they did not push it over the line.

He claims the downside of having the belief they could go and win it is that it hurts even more that they did not.

Tuchel has stated the France third-place game “directs the narrative” of what’s coming for England.

Tuchel will be happy with this so far. Very gentle start from the broadcasters.

In a recent development, no questions from the broadcasters about blowing the lead against Argentina and Tuchel’s opinion about the World Cup. Weird.

“The door is always open through performance, behaviour and commitment.”.

Sources indicate that “They had a good start to the season. Now it’s a new competition. Some positions have injuries. Palmer has his numbers back and a point to prove. Trent was never non-selectable and comes in as a right back.”.

We will be hearing from Tuchel very soon. Lots to discuss but the Palmer and Alexander-Arnold call-ups and his World Cup reflections are at the top of the list.

The big ‘loser’ from the World Cup squad in being left out by Thomas Tuchel is Arsenal’s Noni Madueke. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 11:00.
  • Pep Guardiola has made his first visit to Brazilian club Bahia, offering a glimpse into his continuing involvement with Manchester City's global football network several months after leaving his managerial position at the Etihad Stadium.
  • Recent findings suggest that the former Man City manager arrived in Salvador this week alongside Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group (CFG), which has controlled 90% of Bahia's football operations since 2023.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 21 Nov 2026 11:00.

Pep Guardiola has made his first visit to Brazilian club Bahia, offering a glimpse into his continuing involvement with Manchester City's global football network several months after leaving his managerial position at the Etihad Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that the former Man City manager arrived in Salvador this week alongside Ferran Soriano, chief executive of City Football Group (CFG), which has controlled 90% of Bahia's football operations since 2023. The trip forms part of Guardiola's responsibilities as a global ambassador for the organisation, a position he assumed following his departure from the Premier League club in May.

It has been revealed that guardiola visited Bahia's Cidade Tricolor training complex on Friday, November 20, where he was welcomed by head coach Rogério Ceni and given a tour of the facilities. The 55-year-old also watched a training session ahead of Saturday's Brazilian Serie A encounter with Coritiba, which he is scheduled to attend at the Arena Fonte Nova.

In a recent development, the visit marks a significant moment in Guardiola's relationship with Bahia, a club he first publicly embraced before its integration into City Football Group was completed. Although he is no longer responsible for Manchester City's first team, his presence in Brazil illustrates how the organisation continues to involve its former manager in activities across its international network.

Guardiola's interest in Bahia dates back to 2022, when the club were attempting to secure promotion from Brazil's second division. Before a decisive fixture, he recorded a video message wishing the players success, alongside contributions from other Manchester City representatives.

The relationship developed further after Bahia's supporters approved the club's proposed partnership with CFG in December 2022. The agreement was subsequently completed in May 2023, giving the group a controlling stake in one of Brazil's best-supported clubs.

Speaking in January 2023, Guardiola welcomed the arrangement and expressed his desire to visit Salvador.

According to recent reports, "I'm delighted to know that we're together with them. It was a democratic vote by the supporters, and more than 90% wanted it," he said at the time. "Now invite me so that one day I can go to Brazil, to Bahia, to see them.".

Industry observers note that almost four years later, that invitation has finally been fulfilled. Guardiola's reunion with Ceni on Friday also continued a relationship established when Bahia visited Manchester for pre-season preparations.

According to recent reports, during their earlier meeting, Guardiola praised the former Brazilian goalkeeper, describing him as a "legend" and highlighting his remarkable goalscoring record. Ceni, who scored more than 100 goals during his playing career, has since remained in charge of Bahia as the club attempts to establish itself among Brazil's leading sides.

The Brazilian coach was equally complimentary ahead of Guardiola's arrival, describing the Spaniard as someone who had changed the way football is played.

"It's a pleasure, not just for me but for everyone," Ceni told reporters. "I hope we can produce a performance worthy of having someone of his calibre watching us.".

Guardiola ended his decade-long spell as Manchester City manager at the conclusion of the 2025-26 campaign, closing one of the most successful managerial eras in English football. However, leaving the dugout did not bring his association with City's ownership structure to an end.

As a global ambassador, the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach maintains an institutional connection with CFG, whose portfolio includes clubs such as Girona in Spain, Fresh York City FC in the United States and Montevideo City Torque in Uruguay.

It has been revealed that his journey to Brazil has also included corporate engagements in São Paulo alongside Soriano, before the pair travelled to Salvador for activities associated with Bahia. Their itinerary included the launch of a documentary, O Bahia é o Mundo – A Era City, exploring the Brazilian club's relationship with its international ownership group.

Sources indicate that the visit should not be interpreted as evidence that Guardiola has assumed a formal coaching or recruitment role at Bahia. No such responsibilities have been confirmed, and the activities confirmed during his trip are consistent with his ambassadorial position.

In a recent development, nevertheless, his presence alongside CFG's chief executive demonstrates that Guardiola remains a prominent representative of the organisation beyond his achievements in Manchester. For Bahia, it also provides an opportunity to showcase the club and its facilities to one of the most recognisable figures in world football.

Attention now turns to Saturday's meeting with Coritiba, where Guardiola is expected to watch from the stands as Bahia pursue qualification for next season's Copa Libertadores.

Ceni's team entered the weekend sixth in the Brazilian top flight with 53 points, occupying a position that would at the moment secure a place in the competition's preliminary rounds.

It has been revealed that for Guardiola, the occasion will complete a journey he first discussed publicly in 2023, when he asked Bahia supporters to invite him to Brazil. This time, he will be watching their team in person rather than following its progress from Manchester.

Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1715 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

Strops, scruff, and chaos

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (620 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I watched Man Utd v Aston Villa last night.
  • Sources indicate that this is someone who has managed over 1000 games in his career.
  • In a recent development, meanwhile, it looks as if Pierre Sage is gonna get fired by Crystal Palace and replaced by Thomas Frank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I watched Man Utd v Aston Villa last night. When Villa conceded late on to let a two goal lead slip for the second time in the game, Unai Emery threw a strop and went down the tunnel. It’s not the first time he’s eschewed a handshake with the opposition manager, and his post-game interview where he insisted he thought the game was over was very funny because it was such obvious bullshit.

Sources indicate that this is someone who has managed over 1000 games in his career. I’m pretty sure he knows when the final whistle blows and when it doesn’t. Can you imagine if Mikel Arteta did that? You wouldn’t be able to move for all the opinion pieces about what a sore loser he is and all the rest. But perhaps Emery gets a pass because he is ‘the best manager in the league’. Anyway, perhaps it provides a stay of execution for Michael Carrick at Man Utd, which can only be a good thing.

In a recent development, meanwhile, it looks as if Pierre Sage is gonna get fired by Crystal Palace and replaced by Thomas Frank. That seems a sensible appointment to me. Enough time has passed since his spell at Sp*rs for the toxins to wear off, and he’s clearly a good manager. I’ve never been convinced by Sage, I just think he looks too scruffy. As if someone got a 10 year old to draw man and brought it to life.

I quite enjoyed this quote from Mikel Arteta in his post-game press conference after Saturday’s 1-0 win over Hull:.

Sometimes we try to score the perfect goal against low blocks, but we need to be much more chaotic than that. If we open the scoring much earlier also, it changes the game.

I love it as a concept, adding some chaos to our control makes a lot of sense, but it also kinda seems at odds with what the manager asks of his players. Maybe he just means more shots from distance, maybe riskier pass when we’re trying to break the opposition down, or maybe there’s something he’s got cooking for over the Interlull and when we return we see something we never expected. He did kick the shit out of a dugout chair on Saturday, that’s a newly introduced enough development to be fair.

In a recent development, I wonder was he referring to the Kai Havertz chance in the first half, when he could have shot on his right foot but tried to cut back/lay it off. If you shoot, maybe you don’t score but as we saw with the winning goal from Martin Odegaard, it might end up in the path of another Arsenal player who can finish it off. Perhaps too there’s a bit of a through line between being more chaotic and what Noni Madueke is doing at the moment. He can be a bit scattergun, but as Nick Wright points out on Sky Sports, his numbers are improving. I don’t think Arteta will ever embrace full chaos, all the time, but if he can add a little more to the mix, it could certainly help.

Sources indicate that right, I have to leave it there for this morning. A bit shorter than normal, I know. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around lunchtime. Until then, have a good one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool would have a €23m offer accepted if they make it. The Reds are weighing up a deal that could help transform their season.

Do Liverpool need a upcoming left-back? Really, the question is 'when' - everyone expects Kostas Tsimikas to leave the club at the end of the season when his contract expires.

So it's a matter of what kind of replacement Liverpool opt for. Do they simply want to find a backup player to Milos Kerkez? Or is it a chance to replace him?

There are other possibilities here, too. Liverpool could take advantage of the squad space to find a versatile player who fills a few roles. Or perhaps they want an experienced player who can fit into the leadership group.

Then there's the homegrown question. Liverpool could make things easier for themselves by adding a couple of homegrown players and here's a good opportunity to add one. Should they wish.

Or maybe, above all, they just want an elite left-back who could potentially replace Kerkez as first-choice.

Archie Brown is wanted - and has a clauseTurkish outlet Takvim reports that Liverpool are in the running for Fenerbahçe left-back Archie Brown. The 24-year-old is wanted by several Premier League clubs and for good reason - he's homegrown. Brown made a significant impact against Liverpool this season, of course, as he both scored and assisted in his side's 3-2 win over the Reds. It's something that's catapulted Brown into the spotlight as one to watch, particularly for Premier League sides.

Turkish outlet Takvim reports that Liverpool are in the running for Fenerbahçe left-back Archie Brown. The 24-year-old is wanted by several Premier League clubs and for good reason - he's homegrown.

Brown made a significant impact against Liverpool this season, of course, as he both scored and assisted in his side's 3-2 win over the Reds. It's something that's catapulted Brown into the spotlight as one to watch, particularly for Premier League sides.

The interest is significant enough that we can't imagine the player moves anywhere where he isn't first choice. He's set to have his pick of clubs, too, as a release clause in his contract guarantees that the fee won't get out of hand.

That price is €23m, which is arguably a complete steal for a UEFA Champions League-level left-back right now. Especially one who's English.

We expect Brown to be one of Liverpool's most-wanted in 2027 and there's half a chance that they get the deal done in January. After all, that clause won't be around forever - someone is going to trigger it sooner or later. Another club, then, could force the Reds' hand by making a winter offer.

Absolutely, then, this is one to watch.

Interlull musings and shiny distractions

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1050 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Arseblog

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, we’re two days into the final Interlull of the year and, as you might expect, there’s not a huge amount going on.
  • This time around, 20 of our 25 first-team players have been selected, which is a pretty remarkable tally.
  • Recent findings suggest that any concerns about the Frenchman’s absence against Hull, having travelled to Prague in midweek, were eased the following morning when he lined up for the under-21s against Aston Villa in Premier League 2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we’re two days into the final Interlull of the year and, as you might expect, there’s not a huge amount going on. The senior fixtures don’t start until Thursday, so we haven’t even got a fresh batch of international press conference quotes to sink our teeth into. Slim pickings.

This time around, 20 of our 25 first-team players have been selected, which is a pretty remarkable tally. All the more so when you consider Noni Madueke can count himself unlucky to have missed out for England, while Bukayo Saka and William Saliba would ordinarily be shoo-ins.

Recent findings suggest that any concerns about the Frenchman’s absence against Hull, having travelled to Prague in midweek, were eased the following morning when he lined up for the under-21s against Aston Villa in Premier League 2. More minutes in his legs, rather than another injury to worry about.

Recent findings suggest that bolstered by Saliba and Max Dowman, whose domestic suspension kept him out of Saturday’s game, the youngsters ran out 5-2 winners. Given they’re currently 21st out of 31 teams in their Swiss-style league table, perhaps this is the way forward. Send the big guns down a level and start battering our way towards more club silverware. Relentless madman Arteta, finding latest frontiers for his evil genius. He doesn’t just leave his technical area. He thinks outside it.

According to recent reports, if you missed it, Max has been promoted to England’s under-21s for this window. He’ll join Arsenal loanees Tommy Setford and Ethan Nwaneri, as well as former Hale Enders Brooke Norton-Cuffy, who came off the bench for Hull on Saturday, and Amario Cozier-Duberry, who seems to be doing well at Middlesbrough on loan from Brighton.

Recent findings suggest that given Max has been in and around Mikel Arteta’s first team for a couple of seasons now, it’s easy to take milestones like this for granted. But playing under-21 international football at 16 is another significant step, even for someone whose talent has made rapid progress seem almost routine.

Sources indicate that back in September, Lee Carsley described his eventual promotion as inevitable, while stressing that the timing had to be right. The point was to bring him into a squad where he could play and compete, rather than move him up simply because everyone expected it.

Recent findings suggest that carsley referenced Nwaneri when discussing the temptation to push exceptional youngsters through the age groups. His point was that the aim is a long senior career, not winning a race to the first cap. That seems sensible enough. Max doesn’t need every appearance to become an audition for the next level.

A couple of games against Portugal and France should be a useful challenge in their own right. Carsley and Arteta also know each other from their Everton days, which ought to help when discussing what he needs.

With England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland hosting Euro 2028, you can imagine that tournament already features somewhere in Max’s ambitions. There’s plenty of football between now and then, though. For the moment, let’s see how he gets on with this next step.

It has been revealed that elsewhere, most of our European internationals will be occupied with the Nations League, while the South American trio rack up the air miles again. Piero Hincapie heads home to Ecuador for friendlies against Costa Rica and Bolivia, while Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes face Japan and Singapore, both in Singapore.

I appreciate Brazil’s options are more limited when European teams are tied up with UEFA fixtures, but their friendly schedule does sometimes feel like somebody has thrown a dart at a map. No doubt the commercial logic is compelling, but that doesn’t make you any less worried about tired hamstrings.

Anyway, fingers crossed they all come back with their limbs intact.

Recent findings suggest that in other news, Italian publication Tuttosport has named Andrea Berta the winner of its Best Executive Award at this year’s Golden Boy Awards. The Arsenal sporting director collects the gong three transfer windows into his tenure, the latest of which ended with some fans calling for his head after the failed pursuits of Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez.

Either the bar is pretty low, he’s basking in the reflected glory of the team’s success, or it’s one of those shindigs where buying an inordinately expensive table guarantees you something shiny to take home. The cynic in me wasn’t exactly silenced by the news that Joan Laporta won Best President and Jorge Mendes Best Agent. In fact, I snorted when I read that. And lest we forget, Edu picked up a similar award from the same organisers in 2023….

In a recent development, myles Lewis-Skelly was in contention for the actual Golden Boy award, which went to Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi. Hard to argue too much with that, given the 19-year-old was at the heart of Spain’s World Cup win.

Industry observers note that cubarsi also made the FIFPRO World 11. More pertinently for us, so did David Raya. Having finished second to compatriot Unai Simon in the Ballon d’Or’s Best Goalkeeper category, I imagine there’s some satisfaction in getting the nod from the people who actually play the game. More than 26,000 professionals from 75 countries cast their votes, which is a fairly substantial dressing room to win over.

Alessia Russo, who is in fine form even if Arsenal Women are not, also earned her third selection for the Women’s World 11.

According to recent reports, as you’ll have gathered from the snippiness above, I find it easy to be cynical about these things. There are so many awards now that you half expect to get one for finding your seat at the ceremony. Still, sometimes it’s nice to give people a pat on the back and recognise a job well done.

According to recent reports, on an entirely unrelated note, have you voted for us to win Best Fan Media at the upcoming FSA Awards? You’ve only got a week left. A prestigious honour, that one. 😉.

Right, I think that’s as much toothpaste as I can squeeze out of a slow news day. If anything else happens, we’ll have it covered on Arseblog News. Catch you next time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 21 Nov 2026 11:18, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 11:35.
  • Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki have both been left out of Manchester City’s starting lineup for this afternoon’s Premier League fixture against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium.
  • The Citizens are seeking to bounce back from a run of three successive top-flight defeats, most recently losing 3-1 away against Nottingham Forest before the international break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 21 Nov 2026 11:18, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 11:35.

Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki have both been left out of Manchester City’s starting lineup for this afternoon’s Premier League fixture against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium.

The Citizens are seeking to bounce back from a run of three successive top-flight defeats, most recently losing 3-1 away against Nottingham Forest before the international break.

Manager Enzo Maresca has made a total of three changes to the side that were beaten at the City Ground, with Fernandez, Cherki and Josko Gvardiol all dropping down to the substitutes’ bench.

While Cherki scored in the defeat to Forest, Gvardiol was at fault for a first-half goal conceded by City and Fernandez’s position in midfield has come under question in recent weeks.

Ayyoub Bouaddi will start just his third Premier League game at the expense of Fernandez, while Phil Foden and Nico O'Reilly have been brought in for Cherki and Gvardiol respectively.

While Matheus Nunes missed out through injury, Abdukodir Khusanov has shaken off a knock to start at right-back, joining O'Reilly, Marc Guehi and Ruben Dias in a four-man defence protecting goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Bouaddi will links arms with Elliot Anderson in centre-midfield, with Foden set to operate in the number 10 role between wingers Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku.

Leading the line is goal machine Erling Haaland, who has scored eight goals in as many games against Fulham and is looking to net his 10th Premier League goal of the campaign this afternoon.

As for Fulham, head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has also made a total of three changes to the team that rescued a 1-1 draw with Newcastle United a fortnight ago.

The headline alteration see Gonzalo Garcia begin as a substitute for the first time since joining the Cottagers in the summer following a run of nine straight starts without a goal.

Rodrigo Muniz, who scored a late equaliser off the bench against Newcastle, has been rewarded with his first league start of the campaign at Garcia’s expense.

In a recent development, arbeloa has also opted to change his full-backs, with Kenny Tete and Ryan Sessegnon coming in for Timothy Castagne and Antonee Robinson. Calvin Bassey and David Affengruber retain their places at centre-back, though.

Man City academy graduates Shea Charles and Oscar Bobb both start against their former club, with the former to play alongside Sander Berge in midfield and the latter continuing on the right flank.

Manchester City starting lineup: Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly; Bouaddi, Anderson; Ndiaye, Foden, Doku; Haaland.

Subs: Rulli, Kovacic, Cherki, Fernandez, Reis, Gvardiol, Allan, F. Samba, Lewis.

Fulham starting lineup: Leno; Tete, Affengruber, Bassey, Sessegnon; Berge, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Muniz.

Subs: Kaiser, Castagne, Cuenca, Robinson, Larsson, Cairney, Angel, Palacios, Garcia.

Bloodthirsty Brighton feast on rattled Arsenal

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents.
  • Recent findings suggest that in the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns.
  • Industry observers note that brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Overpowered and overrun, Arsenal were subjected to the sort of gruelling treatment they usually inflict on their opponents. Mikel Arteta’s side did not look anything like Premier League champions here, as Brighton and Hove Albion produced a stunning performance full of swarming energy and breathless bravery.

Recent findings suggest that in the biggest test of their season so far, Arsenal fell woefully short of the standards they have set themselves over the past few campaigns. This sort of thing simply does not happen to Arteta’s side. Well, it did not happen. Not before this monstering on the south coast, where the Brighton fans were whipped into a frenzy by the brilliance of Fabian Hürzeler’s players.

Industry observers note that brighton were everything that Arsenal are expected to be: aggressive, inventive and dominant across the field. They even scored with a set-piece, as one of Arsenal’s great strengths became a sudden weakness. Everywhere Arteta looked, the foundational truths of his team were being shaken by a Brighton storm. It was their first defeat by a three-goal margin since May 2023, also against Brighton.

In a recent development, remarkably, this is now the third consecutive season in which Brighton have beaten the reigning Premier League champions. They are rarely happier than when they are on the hunt against more illustrious opponents, working as a team to snap at heels and then attacking in numbers. They are known as the Seagulls, but they played more like a pack of bloodthirsty wolves. The ferocity of their off-the-ball work, especially in the first half, was extraordinary.

Not for a long time have Arsenal been as rattled as they were here. David Raya misplaced passes, Gabriel Magalhães lost duels and Bruno Guimarães chased the ball in vain. It was Brighton’s Pascal Gross, rather than Arsenal’s Martin Odegaard, who shaped the game in midfield. It was Brighton’s Charalampos Kostoulas, rather than Arsenal’s Kai Havertz, who offered incisive class in attack.

Industry observers note that gross and Kostoulas both struck from range in a one-sided first half, before Chema Andrés added the third after the break. At half-time, Arteta had sprinted down the tunnel towards the dressing room. Whatever messages he gave to his players, they either did not sink in or did not work. By the end, Arsenal were lucky the scoreline was not even more humiliating.

Sources indicate that arteta’s players had come through some tricky assignments in winning their first seven matches of this season, but this was their toughest test yet and they failed it badly. They did not handle the emotions of the occasion particularly well, either: in stoppage time, a frustrated Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouyé. He was perhaps fortunate to avoid a red card.

Recent findings suggest that it was the first time that Rice and Guimarães had started alongside each other for Arsenal and it rapidly became clear that their £180m partnership will need some work. Arsenal would have hoped their experience in the Premier League would allow for an instant connection but, evidently, that is not the case. Guimarães was hooked after 60 minutes, but might easily have been removed at the break.

According to recent reports, both managers had a similar assessment of the match and how it was won: Brighton did the basics far better than Arsenal. “How we wanted to approach this game was getting into it through small wins,” Hürzeler said. “Everyone speaks about a goal or chance as a win, but a small win can be the first throw-in, the first corner, win the first header, win the first tackle. These small things. If you win these small steps, and celebrate them as a win, then you can gain bigger and bigger wins.”.

Sources indicate that it was typical of Brighton that one of their new signings produced an excellent performance in midfield. Andrés, a 21-year-old Spaniard signed from Stuttgart at the end of the transfer window, looks to be the latest gem identified by their data-led recruitment model. No one inside the Amex Stadium was thinking about Carlos Baleba, sold to Manchester United, when Andrés made his tackles and won his headers.

Another upcoming signing, centre-back Luka Vuskovic, was similarly impressive at the back. Signed for £46m from Tottenham Hotspur, Vuskovic looks more than capable of going to the top of the game.

In a recent development, this was perhaps the first occasion this season in which Arsenal missed William Saliba, the injured centre-back who has been so fundamental to their success in recent years. The Frenchman can always be relied on to provide calmness and composure at the back, even under intense pressure. Without him, Arsenal were uncharacteristically jittery.

“The amount of technical errors we did in our own half...” Arteta bemoaned. “We didn’t respect any principle of play that you have to get out of those man-to-man situations. That put us always on the back foot.”.

In a recent development, gross, who at 35 is playing as well as ever, opened the scoring with a low shot from range after 31 minutes. Kostoulas then struck the second, from a similar distance, after some end-to-end action resulted in Arsenal’s midfield and defence melting away. The third was the most simple, as Andrés headed in at the back post from an inswinging corner.

Sources indicate that arsenal did have some chances, with Havertz missing the best of them, but there was never a sense that Brighton were vulnerable. The pressure on the home side was never sustained. For Arteta, who now has an extended international break in which to ruminate on this defeat, it all made for an unfamiliar and unexpected pain.

Mikel Arteta said his Arsenal players failed to “respect the game” as their perfect start to the season was ended in stunning style by a brilliant Brighton performance.

Arsenal’s capitulation on the south coast led to their first defeat of the campaign and Arteta admitted that Brighton had a different “edge” and “bite” throughout the match. The Arsenal manager also noted the 3-0 loss represented a “significant lesson” for his players.

Recent findings suggest that “There are certain basics you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from,” Arteta stated. “From the first throw-in you could sense it, it was so clear.

In a recent development, “It was a really disappointing result and performance. Brighton were another gear up from us. We were extremely poor technically and were not respecting the game.

It has been revealed that “It is not going to take away what the team has done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup. What we have done and the way we have competed, and the amount of games we have won, has been remarkable. But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”.

Arteta added that his team did not “respect the principles of play” that were required against Brighton’s intense pressing, and also said his players were guilty of numerous technical errors.

“Credit to Brighton for what they have done because they have overcome us and they had another edge,” Arteta stated. “There are a lot of moments when the ball is 50/50 and it changes hands and most of the time it was for them.”.

Brighton are the Premier League’s top scorers this season with 16 goals in five matches so far, and this emphatic victory took them up to third place in the table.

“It was a special win,” Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton head coach, said. “Not only because we played the best team in England but because of the performance. I am really proud of my team. It’s always notable to enjoy these moments. We were horrible to play against. My players really trust each other on the pitch.”.

#71941. Inside Newcastle United's transfer tension: Matthias Jaissle wants greater control as he eyes a upcoming No 10 and No 9 in January - but the next four fixtures could make or break him and the club's season, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (972 w)

Inside Newcastle United's transfer tension: Matthias Jaissle wants greater control as he eyes a upcoming No 10 and No 9 in January - but the next four fixtures could make or break him and the club's season, writes CRAIG HOPE

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (972 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail
