⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mikel Arteta’s press conference takes place early this morning, rather than the typical 1.30pm start time.
  • Recent findings suggest that so, the talking points will come later, if there are any talking points.
  • Industry observers note that also, the bloke from Sky Sports will come to the press conference dressed up as a PS5 controller to ask if the manager is concerned about his players staying up all night to to play Grand Theft Auto 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Arteta’s press conference takes place early this morning, rather than the typical 1.30pm start time. I woke up a bit later than usual, and there’s part of me that wonders if I should wait for it before doing the blog, but then that would make the blog a lot later than usual and I don’t want to disrupt anybody’s routine. Especially on a Friday.

Recent findings suggest that so, the talking points will come later, if there are any talking points. My guesses on questions today:.

Industry observers note that also, the bloke from Sky Sports will come to the press conference dressed up as a PS5 controller to ask if the manager is concerned about his players staying up all night to to play Grand Theft Auto 6. Hopefully he requires a firmware update before speaking.

Recent findings suggest that so, in the absence of news and stuff to talk about, I thought I’d point you in the direction of some stuff elsewhere. In a week where we’ve been handing out new contracts all over the place, Phil Costa wonders about the future of Kai Havertz and whether new terms might be on offer for him.

Recent findings suggest that it’s an interesting one because I think it’s clear he’s the manager’s first preference from the two strikers he has available to him. If he was forced to drive deep into the woods and leave one tied to a tree, it’d be Viktor Gyokeres left in the dark forest to try and undo his knots and make his way back to civilisation. But reservations about Kai’s fitness are more than understandable, and while this is a player who has scored big goals for this club since his arrival, there are inconsistencies to his game that can be frustrating.

It has been revealed that he turns 28 in June, which is far from over the hill, but it’s then about the cost of a multi-year commitment to a player who, more than likely, you’re probably never going to get much of a return on. Particularly if you have to add to what is already a significant weekly wage packet, even if others will have taken over the mantle of Arsenal’s best-paid player.

It has been revealed that my gut feeling is that we’ll probably keep him though, and jokes aside it probably is connected to Gyokeres. The Swedish international feels like the player most expendable of the two in the manager’s mind, and I just can’t really see any scenario when simply Arsenal hang onto both for another season or two, or decide that both can be sold and then replaced at the same time. We sold two left-wingers and a striker this summer and replaced them with one single player, so it’s not as if our track record of augmenting the squad in forward areas would give you much confidence in our ability to undergo sweeping reform.

Thus, some consistency will be necessary, and if push comes to shove, Arteta will sell Gyokeres a hundred times before Havertz once – unless there’s something to do with fitness/injury. The question then is do we renew now, or see where we are next summer? If we add a younger striker to the mix, the benefit of Havertz’s experience isn’t to be underestimated, and then in those final 12 months, if there’s a deal to be done it can be done, and if not, the club have time to consider other options. At that point, he’ll be almost 29, he’ll have options elsewhere if there’s no future at Arsenal.

Of course players want some security when it comes to their contracts and their futures, it might be a case he wants that and that may force the glitch one way or the other, but as it stands, it doesn’t seem to be an issue that absolutely has to be a top priority right now (unlike someone like Declan Rice, for example).

For more good reading this morning, Lewis writes about Thomas Frank and Mauricio Pochettino (the major lumpy prick), and the challenges they face with their new clubs. I know I said this on the Arsecast Extra earlier in the week, but I really feel like the latter escapes the scrutiny he deserves for the evil he has perpetrated throughout his career. Manager of Sp*rs, Chelsea and PSG, and now Man Utd, as well as a stint as a national manager during which I thought he thoroughly shamed himself over the Folarin Balogun incident in the World Cup. I know he’s a big mate of Mikel Arteta, but for me he’s up there with the worst of them. A Maroon5 cover of a Phil Collins song brought to life.

Right, I’ll leave it there. As I remarked yesterday, we’ll have a preview podcast over on Patreon later on, but in the absence of an Arsecast this week we’ll make it available to everyone for free via the usual podcast channels. That should be out after lunch at some time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:55 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 09:55 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • St Mirren manager Craig McLeish claims self-interest and poor governance are killing Scottish football’s hopes of improvement.
  • McLeish is frustrated that Scottish Football Association chief football officer Craig Mulholland has reportedly had to dilute plans for young player quotas to appease five William Hill Premiership clubs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:55 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 09:55 EST, 20 November 2026.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish claims self-interest and poor governance are killing Scottish football’s hopes of improvement.

McLeish is frustrated that Scottish Football Association chief football officer Craig Mulholland has reportedly had to dilute plans for young player quotas to appease five William Hill Premiership clubs.

Mulholland was hoping to ensure teams featured Scotland Under-21 eligible players for an average of 60 minutes per league game and had two on the pitch for each cup tie.

McLeish stated: 'That’s damning that he’s having to change his plans to pander to clubs who aren’t really on board with it and don’t really have the best interests of the Scottish national team at heart.

Recent findings suggest that 'I understand why. We have owners from outwith this country. We have managers from outwith this country. They’re in jobs, they’re all fighting for their clubs.

'But why then are those people allowed to be the ones that hold the keys to the future of our country and the development of our national team?

St Mirren boss Craig McLeish believes self-interest at clubs is hampering Scottish football.

'It’s the way governance is set up and we’ve killed ourselves with that because the people who actually have a say in it have, not have no interest but they’ve got self-interest, and there’s a lot of self-interest at the top end.

'I just don’t see a way that we can really properly change unless something to do with governance changes and I just don’t ever see that happening. It’s really sad.'.

Although McLeish backs quotas, he fears that would not address the root cause of Scottish football’s problems.

'We always focus at the top end, what our league size is, quotas for young players, a national base,' said the 36-year-old, who worked in St Mirren’s youth academy before his current role.

'We have a fundamental problem that starts at our youngest age groups, at four and five years of age, about how we actually teach kids to play. And until you fix that, you can’t fix the top end of it.

Sources indicate that 'It’s crazy some of the stuff that’s going on, the formats, how we teach kids. There’s just a massive lack of education and expertise at the very bottom of our pathway.

'In this country, football’s everyone’s sport and everyone gets access to it but if you take your young kids along to swimming or gymnastics or whatever other sport, you’re there with properly qualified coaches, teachers who have maybe done things at the top levels of that sport.

'We have nothing without the volunteers that work at the bottom end of the grassroots game, but they’re not teaching kids how to play football properly, in my mind.

'And you’re just hoping that they get put with a volunteer coach that can teach them something, that they get in with a really good group at the youngest ages.

'Because that development between the ages of three and eight, if you don’t get that right, you’re dead. You can’t do anything after that point, and we don’t do it well enough. And you’re just chasing yourself and we’ll never catch up.'.

The SFA has been contacted for comment.

#71892. Opinion: Liverpool ready to sign their next Jeremy Jacquet, he's perfect

Opinion: Liverpool ready to sign their next Jeremy Jacquet, he's perfect

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The young Frenchman was brought in for around £55 million with plenty of fans, pundits and journalists all saying that Liverpool had spent too much on a player who'd never played outside of France.
  • The fact that he was only 20 years old didn't help matters much either.
  • However, to the surprise of many, he took becoming a Liverpool player in his stride and has arguably been one of their best performers this term.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jeremy Jacquet has been a revelation at Liverpool.

The young Frenchman was brought in for around £55 million with plenty of fans, pundits and journalists all saying that Liverpool had spent too much on a player who'd never played outside of France.

The fact that he was only 20 years old didn't help matters much either.

However, to the surprise of many, he took becoming a Liverpool player in his stride and has arguably been one of their best performers this term.

He's far better than Ibrahima Konate ever was and, he's still got another decade left as a top-level player.

So, the fact that Liverpool are ready to sign their next version of him is rather exciting.

Liverpool have entered the transfer race for Giorgio Scalvini.

Liverpool's defence may have had a decent chunk of change spent on it over the last couple of years but, there are still a couple of problem areas that they need to fix.

For example, both Kostas Tsimikas and Milos Kerkez have massively underperformed this season.

Every time one of them is played, fans want the other to come back in and take their place.

Obviously, this isn't ideal considering Kerkez was expected to be the Reds' next Andy Robertson.

However, the centre of their defence also has a couple of question marks hanging over it thanks to the undecided futures of Virgil van Dijk and Joe Gomez.

So, Liverpool being linked with Giorgio Scalvini is hardly a surprised, especially with how much potential he has to fulfil.

"Manchester United, Liverpool and Chelsea are positioning themselves to make a possible move for Atalanta defensive star Giorgio Scalvini, with the highly-rated Italian emerging as a major potential transfer target for 2027, TEAMtalk can exclusively reveal," TEAMtalk wrote.

"TEAMtalk understands that a number of English sides are now carrying out detailed work on Scalvini as the possibility of him finally leaving Atalanta gathers momentum.

"Newcastle United are long-term admirers of the Italy international, but the latest interest is coming from Manchester United, Liverpool and Chelsea, who have all been monitoring his development.

"United and Liverpool are both assessing their central defensive options as they consider potential reinforcements, with Scalvini increasingly emerging as a player of interest to their recruitment departments.".

Giorgio Scalvini could become Liverpool's next Jeremy Jacquet.

Scalvini has been linked with an exit from Atalanta for a fair few years now.

Ever since he broke into their first team back in the 2021/22 season, the Italian has been of interest to many different clubs around the globe.

However, now that Liverpool have proven that they're giving youngsters a go in their starting XI with their use of Jacquet and others such as Trey Nyoni, they have more ground to stand on than other clubs.

Of course, Scalvini is a tad older than Jacquet at 22 years old but, since they're both young and have a lot of their careers left to go, it's clear to see why the Italian could become Liverpool's next Jacquet.

He also plays as the right-sided centre-back in a back four so, he'd fit straight into Andoni Iraola's prepares if they chose to bring him in.

#71891. Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5549 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3. This prevailing view, however, masks substantial fine-scale variation in leaf phenology, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to climate change. Here by combining 10-m Sentinel-2 observations with machine learning, we uncover pervasive, spatially structured seasonal deciduousness across the basin. In 70.0% of the Amazon, leaf shedding precedes leaf flushing by at least 3 months, creating pronounced asynchrony between deciduousness and greenness seasonality, whereas the remainder shows near-synchronous phenology. Hydroclimate emerges as the dominant factor associated with this asynchrony across 51.6% of the area, followed by soil properties (33.2%) and light availability (15.2%). Motivated by this widespread decoupling between deciduousness and canopy greenness, we incorporated deciduousness-constrained leaf turnover and the resulting leaf-age demography into ecophysiological models, yielding spatially widespread improvements in the seasonal agreement between simulated gross primary productivity and satellite-derived photosynthetic seasonality across 79.9% of the basin. These findings challenge the conventional view of Amazonian phenology, demonstrating that previously overlooked deciduousness influences Amazonian carbon dynamics. Incorporating these insights into process-based models is essential for refining projections of climate–forest feedbacks in the Amazon and for understanding its ecological functions under accelerating global change.

Recent findings suggest that symbols indicate data sources, including sites with (1) both eddy-covariance flux and phenocam observations (n = 3; green stars); (2) eddy-covariance flux only (n = 1; blue star); (3) phenocam observations only (n = 2; yellow stars); (4) litterfall observations (n = 47; red triangles); (5) inventory plots (n = 289; purple circles); and (6) very high-resolution Google Earth image locations (n = 16; 0.5-m spatial resolution, each covering a 2 km × 2 km area; blue squares). Site information, including location, data type, and observation period, is provided in Supplementary Table 1. The map was created using ArcGIS Pro with the Esri World Ocean Base basemap. Basemap sources: Esri, Garmin, GEBCO, NOAA NGDC and other contributors.

Recent findings suggest that panels a-e compare the temporal dynamics of ecosystem-scale deciduousness fraction from Sentinel-2 (blue line) with the fraction of leafless tree crowns visually assessed from phenocam images (black line). The Sentinel-2 deciduousness fraction is calculated as the mean value within a 500 m × 500 m area centred on each phenocam site, while the phenocam typically covers an area of approximately 100 m × 100 m. Panel f demonstrates the relationship between Sentinel-2-derived deciduousness and the corresponding deciduousness derived from phenocam observations across five sites (n = 60 paired site-month observations). The solid line indicates an ordinary least-squares linear regression, with statistical significance assessed using a two-sided test (p = 6.17 × 10−22).

Recent findings suggest that a, Relationship between standardized monthly litterfall and standardized satellite-derived deciduousness across annual cycles at 47 Amazonian sites (n = 559 pooled site-month observations). The red line indicates the ordinary least-squares linear regression across all pooled data, and the inset boxplot summarizes the site-level distribution of correlation coefficients (r, n = 47 sites). b, Relationship between satellite-derived deciduousness amplitude and the ground-derived proportion of deciduous tree species across the Amazon basin. Grey circles represent raw plot-to-pixel observations (n = 289 plots). The red line shows the ordinary least-squares linear fit to the raw observations, and the shaded band indicates the 95% confidence interval of the fitted mean relationship. The dashed grey line indicates the 1:1 relationship. For a and b, statistical significance of the regression slopes was assessed using two-sided tests (a, p = 2.52 × 10−141; b, p = 7.24 × 10−28). The p values were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. c, Patch-level comparison of deciduousness derived from Sentinel-2 (y-axis) against that derived from closely date-matched, high-resolution Google Earth imagery (GEI; x-axis) via image-specific Random Forest classification and pooled across all 16 validation scenes. Each dot represents a 100-m × 100-m aggregated patch (n = 6058 patches), and the dashed black line marks the 1:1 relationship. d, e, Scene-level distributions of correlation coefficients (r; d) and root-mean-square errors (RMSE; e) calculated separately for each of the 16 GEI validation scenes. Grey dots represent individual scenes. In all boxplots, the centre line indicates the median, the box bounds the interquartile range (IQR), and the whiskers extend to 1.5 × IQR.

a, c, e, g, Spatial maps of evergreen forest cover (a), MODIS Vegetation Continuous Fields tree cover (c), EVI amplitude (e) and VOD amplitude (g). Inset histograms show the basin-wide frequency distribution of each metric. b, d, f, h, Corresponding pixel-level relationships between Sentinel-2-derived deciduousness amplitude and the four reference metrics. Hexbin colour indicates observation density, and dashed lines indicate least-squares linear regressions. Sample sizes (b, d, f, h) were n = 227,612, 227,612, 226,942 and 221,884 valid paired forest pixels, reflecting product-specific data availability. All two-sided tests gave p < 10−300. Correlation coefficients (r) and regression equations are shown in each panel.

Panels a-h show how each variable affects deciduousness–greenness asynchrony, with positive SHAP values (>0) indicating a positive effect and negative SHAP values (<0) indicating a negative effect. The black line in each panel represents a fitted line, summarizing the central tendency of the data points.

Bar charts show the proportional influence of hydroclimate, soil, and light for the entire basin (a), Southern Amazon (b), Guiana Shield (c), and Everwet Amazon (d).

Recent findings suggest that a-c, Spatial patterns of model-performance gain, expressed as the change in the correlation coefficient (Δr) between the GPP seasonality simulated by LD-LUE and that simulated by each corresponding conventional LUE model, with both evaluated against satellite SIF. Results are shown for the EC-LUE (a), two-leaf EC-LUE (TL-EC-LUE; b) and MODIS-LUE (c). Positive Δr indicates better agreement of LD-LUE with satellite SIF relative to its conventional counterpart. Insets show the basin-wide distributions of Δr, with the red dashed line marking Δr = 0 and the annotated values indicating the percentage of forest pixels with Δr > 0.

Italy’s U21 head coach, Silvio Baldini, has shared his thoughts on the Milan trio Alphadjo Cisse, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi.

In recent years, Milan have shifted more towards giving some of their academy graduates more playing time with the first team. Bartesaghi was the first to properly get in, cementing his spot in the starting eleven last season, while Cisse has been the significant breakthrough this season.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Camarda has had a tougher time after a loan spell at Lecce, but Milan have made it very clear through renewals and words that they will focus more on the youngsters. It’s exciting times as well, given how they have all performed with the U21 national team too.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Italy’s U21 coach Silvio Baldini was asked about the breakthrough of Cisse, Camarda’s current state of mind and why Bartesaghi is a ‘luxury’ for his team. Safe to say that he likes the trio a lot.

Industry observers note that cisse has had a proper breakthrough. Did you see that coming?

“Compared to a year ago, I can see a different guy, who’s more mature and prepared, with higher self-esteem, psychologically changed, simply stronger.

“He has Milan to thank for signing him from Catanzaro in Serie B, believing in him and making room for him, then giving him consistent playing time. If he then makes the national team and does well, so much the better.”.

Milan deserve credit, and you also deserve credit for discovering him as a centre-forward….

It has been revealed that “Analysing training sessions, a series of situations emerged where he managed to score by attacking space and depth: if you can do it on the right and left, it means you can also do it in the centre. But even there, the credit goes entirely to the staff.

It has been revealed that “They had the intuition, realising that Cisse could be useful to our game system in that way and at the same time, allowing Alpha to discover a upcoming role successfully. I’m simply honest and meritocratic in my choices.

“Even though the goal against Armenia actually came from him as a second striker, at the end of that match we had two centre-forwards, him and Camarda.”.

In a recent development, camarda, by the way, has struggled at Milan but scored for the U21s. How is that possible?

According to recent reports, “I can only speak about the work we do together. I spoke to him at length, I dedicated time to him, I asked him to explain his concerns, his fear of not being able to express himself as he would like. I told him stories of my own life, of how I came out of it.

“A dialogue not as a coach-player but as a son, or rather a grandson, as he could be, and a grandfather: from the heart. I’m not interested in performances as an end in themselves; they will come if he feels in the right place.

“I try to make him understand that I see him, I follow him in many small ways: he’s a conscientious boy who shouldn’t become obsessed with the goal, but rather experience football for what it is: fun.

“If, instead of fun, it becomes a test, then it worries you, and if you worry, you no longer enjoy it and it doesn’t help you perform at your best.”.

To have more fun, do you recommend that he should leave Milan for another team?

It has been revealed that “I’m not going to get involved in this. There are clubs, agents, and a family: they know what the best path will be for him. Let’s remember that he’s 18 years old, he plays for AC Milan and in the Under-21s.

In a recent development, “It’s clear that the more he plays, the better it will be for AC Milan and for everyone. We’re talking about a great player, a champion in my opinion, who needs to finish his development: he’s still growing, he already has a great eye for goal, and he’s sacrificing himself for the team.”.

Camarda-Cisse: Can Milan provide the national team with one of the forward duos of the future?

“For me, yes. I see them as a permanent fixture in the national team, and of course they need to prove it and earn it on the pitch. But they have all the characteristics to do it. I found Alpha to be better prepared, even in his game decisions. Amorim did well to develop him.”.

The third Rossoneri player is Bartesaghi: more of a full-back like with you or a winger like at Milan?

“Davide is one of the best players in his position I’ve coached in many years. He’s talented, very professional, mature, introverted yet open, and that’s not a contradiction: he has enormous potential, and he demonstrates it every time he comes to us.

According to recent reports, “If I were any Serie A coach, I’d take him with me. For the Under-21s, Bartesaghi is a luxury. He plays with heart, passion, and intelligence, as well as possessing high-level technical, physical, and running skills.

“He can play in any position on the flank. In my opinion, if he starts 50 meters from the goal, he can perform at his best.”.

Tech Report: Newcastle a challenge but a good post-Interlull opportunity

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal are back in Premier League action after the Interlull with a trip to face Newcastle away from home.
  • Industry observers note that in terms of the Arsenal team today, Arteta can flip a coin between Ben White and Jurrien Timber, both of whom were on the scoresheet for their countries during the break.
  • In midfield there’s no Martin Zubimendi whose unfortunate run of injuries continues with a hamstring strain picked up playing for Spain against England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal are back in Premier League action after the Interlull with a trip to face Newcastle away from home. It’s been a difficult place to visit over the years, and we’ve had some unenjoyable encounters – there particularly during Eddie Howe’s tenure. However, Mikel Arteta more or less has a full squad to choose from, and this version of Newcastle under newly introduced manager Matthias Jaissle haven’t been at all convincing so far this season.

Industry observers note that in terms of the Arsenal team today, Arteta can flip a coin between Ben White and Jurrien Timber, both of whom were on the scoresheet for their countries during the break. My gut feeling is that the Dutchman will start today with White penciled in for Borussia Dortmund in midweek. William Saliba is back after another behind closed doors appearance to build his fitness, but for a game that’s likely to be intense and physical, I can’t see anything other than Ezri Konsa alongside Gabriel today. The Frenchman often needs a game or two to get his rhythm back, and while friendlies are useful, they’re not quite the same as competitive minutes. He too is likely to feature in the Champions League on Tuesday.

In midfield there’s no Martin Zubimendi whose unfortunate run of injuries continues with a hamstring strain picked up playing for Spain against England. The form of Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard means they’re first picks, and then it’s about how the manager views Bruno Guimaraes for a game like this. Even if Newcastle haven’t been great, the pantomime villain in midfield adds a layer of spice that is inevitable after his summer move. If he wants to keep the crowd quiet, he could choose Myles Lewis-Skelly, but he paid £75m for this player for a good reason, and I think we’ll see the Brazilian from the start.

Industry observers note that he was a hugely key player for Newcastle, and while I don’t think his departure was among the most contentious we’ve ever seen, he will be a target for their fans, and perhaps for players who know him – and his temper – very well. You’d hope at 28 he’s mature enough to deal with all that, and I’m sure conversations will have been had about not rising to any bait. Arteta has stated more than once recently he wants more from this player, where better to give that than his former club?

According to recent reports, as for the front three, I think it will be Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke either side of Kai Havertz. The injury news for Bukayo Saka means he’s going to miss another month, at least, so there’s a substantial onus on Madueke to continue his recent improved form, but we’ll need him to add end product to the one goal and one assist he’s provided in the league so far. Similarly, Tzolis had a bright-ish start to his Arsenal career, and while the hamstring injury was ill-timed, we need a player who is ostensibly our first choice left winger to start delivering more in terms of assists but especially goals.

Havertz got the winner away to Liverpool, but had frustrating moments at home to Hull. He’s got Viktor Gyokeres on the bench to put some pressure on him, but this front three has some convincing to do and today would be a very good day to produce performances and end product.

Industry observers note that arteta was asked if the atmosphere at St James’ Park isn’t quite what it used to be, because of the way the team has changed and the inconsistent form they’ve suffered so far this campaign. His message was clear:.

If that’s the case, it will be even more difficult, because they will be even better prepared, they will have even more necessity to do that, and that’s what we expect. We always expect the best version from the opponent. That’s how we have to prepare for the game, and that’s how we’re going to approach it.

So, there’s no chance he’s letting his team think for a second this might be easier because it’s not the same Newcastle that have caused us problems in recent seasons. Nevertheless, he must have looked at this team and some of the complications they’ve had under their newly introduced manager and recognised that this is an opportunity to go there with a settled side of his own in good form and come away with all three points.

It is always a challenge there, but this is a mature Arsenal that should be capable of dealing with a team that has just three wins from thirteen games in all competitions this season. You never take anything for granted, but if we can keep the ball in the early stages, get control, and perhaps even an early goal, the ingredients are there for us to make this a winning start to what is a tricky run of games over the coming weeks. Fingers crossed.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. As ever, we’ll bring you live blog coverage of the game later, as well all the post-game stuff on Arseblog News like the match report, player ratings, manager reaction, quotes round-up and more. There’s also a preview podcast on Patreon if you need something to listen to ahead of kick off. 💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 21 Nov 2026 13:45, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 13:48.

Bayern Munich and England star Harry Kane has vowed to return for the "business end of the season" after undergoing ankle surgery.

The striker sustained an ankle ligament injury in Bayern's 1-1 draw against FC Koln on Friday evening.

Kane attempted to carry on after being caught in a tackle from Koln defender Joel Schmied before he received treatment and made way for Tom Bischof in the 20th minute.

Bayern released a statement after the game, revealing Kane would be out for a "few months" with a "torn syndesmotic ligament in his left ankle".

In a recent development, in a fresh update on Saturday morning, Bayern said: "Harry Kane underwent successful surgery overnight following the syndesmosis ligament tear in his left ankle, which he sustained in yesterday’s Bundesliga match against 1. FC Köln.

"The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program.".

Kane also shared a defiant message on social media, accompanied by an image of him sitting on a hospital bed with his left foot in a protective boot.

"The highs and lows of life!" Kane wrote. "Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027.

"I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season!

“‘Tough times don’t last, tough people do’ - my guy Julian Edelman (three-time Super Bowl winner) told me this one!

It has been revealed that “Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut!”.

The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season! “Tough times don’t last, tough people do” - my guy @Edelman11 told me this one! Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut! ❤️?

With Kane likely to be out until the end of February, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany will have to come up with solutions to negate the impact of being without his star striker.

Ismael Saibari can play as a centre-forward, but he is at the moment sidelined with the same injury as Kane, putting him out of action until the start of February.

Serge Gnabry is also on the sidelines and is unlikely to be back until the turn of the year, leaving Kompany without another potential candidate to fill the void created by Kane's absence.

Noah Codjo-Evora is an option if Kompany decides to put his faith in youth, but the 19-year-old is unlikely to start regularly given the fact he only made his first-team debut as a substitute on Friday.

That means Kompany will likely opt to field a false nine in the coming weeks and months, which is a role Lennart Karl played when Kane went off against Koln.

#71887. Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change

Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5155 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home.
  • On TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five.
  • "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville states Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, sometimes comments, however over the top, hit home. Michael Carrick will desperately hope the remark from his former Manchester United team-mate Gary Neville is not one of them. That it does not stick. That it does not come to define his time in charge of United this season – if he lasts this season. Or be used in one of those highlight reels, with doom-laden music, to explain the story of this Premier League campaign.

On TV co-commentary duty for Sky, Neville referred to United as “blue mannequins” (they were wearing their away kit) and said that for a period after half-time it was the worst he had ever seen them play since he started watching, aged five. Neville is now 51. That is a lot of games to settle on this conclusion so strongly and, surely, inaccurately.

"They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville states Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

Recent findings suggest that but so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the strategy to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

According to recent reports, that still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

It is not just that. Last year, United revamped their attack. Benjamin Sesko was absent through injury but are Cunha – despite his goal – Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford actually showing they are good enough? They, too, are passive and do not effect the play. Do not have that killer instinct. There is then an over-reliance on Fernandes. And if he does not do it, then who steps up?

That 15 minutes after half-time that culminated in the Martínez mishap was certainly woeful. But despite going close, United were also second best in the opening period, with Fulham’s 19-year-old academy product Josh King showing why he was so close to a senior England call-up. The forward ran riot, tormenting left-back Luke Shaw and was only denied by Senne Lammens. On more than one occasion, especially with a smart save with his right boot.

The goalkeeper was at the centre of Fulham’s goal, which was a shambles that summed up the state of United, who are just too easy to play against. And, so, Fulham’s captain Calvin Bassey was too strong for Cunha, who threw himself to the ground, looking for a foul, losing the ball from Kobbie Mainoo’s easy pass. The defender strode forward before Lammens parried his low shot, which then bounced off Martínez and back past the goalkeeper and into the net.

In a recent development, it was a Hammersmith End House of Horrors for United. To cap it all, Martínez then tried to blame Lammens who had, frankly, kept United in the game up until that point and could legitimately have told him where to go. And asked why he could not trap a ball and clear.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

Fulham will certainly feel their own frustration. But with their newly introduced head coach Álvaro Arbeloa and an evolving team – if only striker Gonzalo García was more deadly – there are clear signs of optimism, having also just drawn at Liverpool.

Industry observers note that united’s late equaliser was fortunate. Yes, they applied pressure but to no real effect until Cunha’s shot deflected off the boot of Fulham defender David Affengruber as he tried to block, to wrong-foot goalkeeper Bernd Leno, who had also been outstanding. It was credited to Cunha, his first of the season, and the relief from Carrick was understandably palpable.

Sources indicate that manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

In a recent development, but, once again, it was not up to the standard needed. And beyond the point, beyond the avoidance of defeat, that is the reality of where United are right now under Carrick who needs to step up, take more responsibility. And, like his team, be far less passive. Otherwise, he will not last.

Might these games offer less possession and more counter-attacking chances? That’s glass half full.

I was purely referring to the fact that they walked around the pitch. I’ve never seen a Manchester United team walk around on the pitch that much.

Michael has got to stop defending them. I get why he wants to defend them, he’s loyal, and there’s a long way to go into the season.

Both teams were the same, I called them mannequins. I’ve never seen United walk around so much out of possession, no alertness, no being on your toes.

I wish he could play those attacking players, but they are going to kill him defensively.

Neville goes on to call that period: “An absolute disgrace, nowhere near good enough.”.

Industry observers note that "They were absolutely mannequins!" Gary Neville notes Michael Carrick has to stop defending the Manchester United players. pic.twitter.com/Pa4PqIoRbh.

I know Manchester United have a lot of individual quality, I have played against them for many years and know them really well. I know to be alert in case they shoot from distance. When you make some saves in the game you feel very focused. Unfortunately I couldn’t keep out the goal but that is football.

I didn’t think we were. Did you think we were? Football is a difficult game. We controlled a lot of the first half. It’s the Premier League and you will have spells where you don’t have it all your own way. To expect total dominance for the whole game, I don’t think anyone gets that in this league.

It has been revealed that I thought we should have won the game, I thought we created enough to win the game. The goal we did concede is one of them goals. The boys could have thought it is one of those days but I really like the reaction. We nearly won it in the end. We came to get the win of course, the way it panned out and the way we finished is the positive we take from it.

I think we did a good game. Obviously not an easy game for us, we were in the bottom position but we saw personality with the ball, we were brave. We had moments where we had to defend but in general we did a good game.

We wanted to control the transition and the counter attacks. We know they put too many people inside so we have to control the space behind our midfielders. They sometimes found the spaces, it is a difficult match against a big team and for me they will be near the top of the league by the end of the season.

Sources indicate that now we have to find the first victory. If you see our first five games we have already played Man Utd, Chelsea, at Anfield, at Sunderland. Now we have an October that will be so important for us.

There were so many things for them, you can see it in the foul by [Harry] Maguire. Every decision was for them. I knew after the game against Manchester City that they don’t like Manchester United to lose.

It’s hard to explain, I feel after the first half we always get a lot of chances and create, play well.

It has been revealed that in the beginning of the second half they put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this. We always play better after conceding goal, and it cannot be like this.

I don’t think today was about final decisions, we were a bit unlucky, I hit the post, and Bruno hit the post. We need to create more and hope the luck comes and we score. We need to improve in every single position.

Recent findings suggest that it was too slow, Fulham ran more and looked like they wanted to win more. Bassey just eased Cunha out the way [for Fulham’s goal] and looked like he wanted to take the game to Man United and Carrick will be thinking ‘we need to do a lot more’.

It was a game that was a real struggle for both teams. Both lacked confidence. There were challenges for both managers coming into this game, they both need the international break to start their seasons again.

The defensive work from both teams was awful and lacked effort. Carrick will be relieved going back to Manchester with a goal and a point.

Manchester United play Spurs when the Premier League returns in three weeks, in a game that will feel huge.

5 - With five points, this is Manchester United's joint-lowest tally after five games of a Premier League season, also picking up five in 2014-15.Sluggish. pic.twitter.com/UZTBWRpGnm.

It has been revealed that fulham remain winless but the draw lifts them above Spurs, who will spend the international break at the foot of the table. It is just one win in five for United, and it was another performance which was far from convincing. It could have been worse though, they were a few minutes away from losing. On this evidence, both of these teams are in for a struggle relative to expectations.

Fulham wanted a free-kick on the edge of the box for a sliding challenge on Kevin for Maguire but the referee decides he got the ball.

In a recent development, united break forward and win a corner. It comes for Martinez who shifts his feet to shoot with his right foot and the goal-bound effort was blocked!

Just the three minutes of added time to play, but United are the team pushing forward searching for an unlikely winner.

United may have just spared themselves a damaging defeat, and there might just be time to go on an win this. Cunha with a speculative shot from outside the box, and Affengruber extends his left leg to block the shot but the deflection leaves Leno stranded. A stroke of luck for United but Fulham have invited it.

Manchester United are LEVEL! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DCxwlrzf1M.

Bassey now penalised for a high boot on Dalot, United free-kick on the halfway line. Fulham just about standing firm, and they are helped when a crossfield pass towards Dorgu bounces off for a throw-in.

According to recent reports, united with another corner and there are loud appeals for a handball penalty against Bassey, the proximity was very close but his hand was up. But VAR takes a look and the fact the hand was tucked in towards his chest spares the Fulham defender.

Sources indicate that fulham and the home crowd happy with a goal kick after an overhit cross towards Shaw at the back post. Dorgu has been sent on in Carrick’s last throw of the dice, replacing Shaw at left-back.

Recent findings suggest that you would not say United are pulling Fulham from pillar to post, it feels a little hopeful, but it is one-way traffic. An attack against defence session in Fulham’s half. Charles and Kevin do well to relieve the pressure momentarily, but United are back on the attack again.

According to recent reports, here are those changes: Mason Mount on for Kobbie Mainoo for United, while Andersen replaces King for the home team. Arbeloa happy to hold what he has. Lisandro Martinez volleys a shot over the bar.

Positive first involvement from Zirkzee, releasing Mbeumo, but the Fulham defenders read his intentions and blocked the shot after he cut inside. Joachim Andersen is preparing to come on for Fulham, as is Mason Mount for United.

Much better from Fulham, another attack started by Bassey reading play just like the goal, but this time Lammens’s wrists were strong to parry Kevin’s shot. Rashford is then flagged offside.

Fulham change: Larsson is on for Berge, Sweden for Norway. And Carrick has brought on Zirkzee for Rashford. Famous last words, but does that make you more likely to score a goal? Not that Rashford can feel hard done to.

Fulham have stopped playing since they scored, and they needed Leno again to tip a Cunha shot around the post. The United forward was falling over, but he generated enough power to trouble the goalkeeper. From the corner, Maguire picks up the ball on the far side and chips a cross over the blue shirts in the middle.

Recent findings suggest that kevin sold himself in a one-on-one with Rashford, but King did well to put his foot in at the edge of the box and the ball bounces through kindly to Leno. Tielemans then misplaces a pass when United were in a promising position.

If United had played like this from the start of the second half they would not be losing, but now they have just 20 minutes plus stoppage time to overturn the deficit.

Fulham making a double sub: Kevin and Palacios on for Iwobi and Bobb.

United have roused themselves since conceding, winning a flurry of corners.

What a save from Leno! Mbeumo’s curling shot from outside the box was arcing beautifully into the far corner, but the German goalkeeper tipped his effort around the post.

Then Maguire is eased out at the back post, and Fulham breathe a sigh of relief.

Strong words from Gary Neville after the goal went it: “I’ve watched United since the age of five and that is the worst 15 minutes [from half-time to the goal] I have seen them play.”.

Well doesn’t that just sum up United’s season so far. There are appeals for a foul on Cunha from Bassey, but the Fulham defender was stronger and he took some initiative to drive towards the box. Bassey let fly and kept his shot down, Lammens could only stick out a leg and the ball rebounded off the helpless Martinez and back into the net.

"A horror at the Hammersmith end!"Lisandro Martínez puts the ball into his own net and Fulham lead! 😯 pic.twitter.com/jDmY4zL2XN.

It has been revealed that fulham have a corner after it opened up nicely for Iwobi at the edge of the box, but his left-footed strike deflects behind. A very smooth footballer, but finishing has never been Iwobi’s strong suit. Fulham fail to make anything of the corner.

It has been revealed that fulham and United’s fans now urging their teams on after the game halted to glacial pace. Nothing much happening at all since the start of the second half.

It has been revealed that gary Neville growing increasingly frustrated by the lack of intensity out of possession by both teams: “Never walk on a football pitch.” Questions have been asked of United’s fitness levels and physical readiness for the newly introduced season. Fulham enjoying a spell of possession in United’s half again.

Industry observers note that more from Neville: “It’s like it’s time for the whites to play against the blue mannequins, before they reverse it up the other end. One thing I do know, I’ve played in a lot of football matches, it’s not right.”.

There has been a real lack of conviction in Rashford’s play in the final third, this time it was underhit pass across the box towards Mbeumo which was cut out. Good ball by Tielemans to release Rashford, but no end product again.

Industry observers note that sir Alex Ferguson is watching on at Craven Cottage. The game has slipped into one of its lulls again.

Nice football from Fulham involving Charles and Iwobi but United break forward after a loose touch by Bobb. Fernandes did well to keep the ball and wait for support, and Castagne is booked for a block on Rashford.

The first few minutes of the half are played deep in Fulham’s territory, but United’s delivery from wide is not good enough and Cunha is penalised for a foul in the middle in any case.

Fulham kick off in the second half.

Industry observers note that at half-time that is another worrying performance from Manchester United. Yes, they could be ahead and have created chances, with Bruno Fernandes hitting the post. But on the balance of play they should be behind with Fulham’s 19-year-old Josh King the best player on the pitch and United reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Michael Carrick has more work to do during the interval than Fulham’s Alvaro Arbeloa and cannot be happy with how defensively vulnerable his team and but also how wasteful they are in front of goal.

Both teams will believe they should have scored in that first half in a game that has oscillated between periods of passivity and flurries of goal-mouth action. When United speed up their interplay, it looks like they can cut through Fulham, but Carrick’s team’s box defending leaves much to be desired. There were 26 shots on goal without reward in that 45 minutes.

Another chance is missed, this time Rashford with a side foot over the bar from a Cunha cross that took a nick on the way through. Always leaning back, poor technique from a player of his standing.

Fulham then throw a punch back, but King is booked for diving after pushing the ball beyond Maguire. The attacker is not happy, but not sure he can have any complaints.

United almost caught out by a one-two between Iwobi and Garcia, but Lammens rushes off his line to get there first. Both attacks look to have the beating of both defences, but somehow there have been no goals.

United’s best move of the game, starting with a whipped pass from Tielemans when under pressure into Dalot who turns into space inside. Fernandes could have taken a shot on himself from the edge of the box, but he moved the ball on to Rashford but his side-foot shot was tame and straight at Leno.

In a recent development, the game has settled after that flurry of chances when both teams could easily have scored. Fulham do well to block Rashford’s sight of goal as he cuts inside looking for a shot, and then Mbeumo commits a foul.

Cunha with a deflected strike from distance, which arcs over Leno and glances off the post! The sort of deflection that gives a goalkeeper no chance, Leno was scrambling.

According to recent reports, mainoo’s shot is blocked from the corner, and then Fulham break forward with numbers. Iwobi picks out Josh King in the box, and Lammens sticks out a right leg to keep out his driven shot.

Josh King is again showing why he was so close to a full England call-up. The 19-year-old is at the heart of the action as Fulham continue to create chance after chance against a very shaky Manchester United defence who have been reliant on goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

Fulham respond, with Robinson’s cross looping to the back post to the unmarked King but he could not get over the side-foot volley and it was a comfortable save from Lammens.

This stop was less comfortable though: Lammens plunges to his right to keep out a dig by Sander Berge from the edge of the box. It came after Garcia kicked fresh air in the area.

Then Bobb collects the ball in space at the edge of the box and is able to turn but he dragged his shot wide.

The home team and crowd have burst into life.

Fernandes hits the post for United! He should score, and it was poor defending from Fulham. Affengruber ran beyond the ball and was rolled by Cunha who was able to drive into the box, and he pulled the ball back for Fernandes who dragged his shot a touch, and it rebounded off the foot of the post.

Bruno Fernandes hits the post! 😬 pic.twitter.com/jMzn8ZyoYa.

Better from United, turning the screw around the Fulham box but neither Mainoo nor Rashford fashion room for a shot, and then Dalot shoots wide from 25 yards with his weaker left foot.

Josh King finding space off the shoulder of United’s midfield again, but his shot from a tight angle is always rising. United are asking for trouble though if Fulham’s most creative player keeps collecting the ball in those spaces.

United then come forward, with Robinson selling himself against Mbeumo, but Rashford cannot get over the header at the back post.

In a recent development, fulham with a smooth passage of play from deep, finding space down United’s right and Garcia had made a dangerous run between Maguire and Martinez. Iwobi looked for his team-mate, but the ball glanced off his foot as he tried to direct it towards goal.

The interesting thing about Manchester United’s attack is that while they are all, clearly, individually good players do they actually do enough to warrant their status at the club? The truth is Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Marcus Rashford simply have to do more and dominate games. We are yet to see that form them this season and, apart from Lisandro Martinez forcing a fine save from Bernd Leno, Fulham have carried the greater threat here.

According to recent reports, fulham have a corner after Josh King used his body well against Shaw. There has been lots of cat and mouse so far, both teams trying to play patiently from deep and the out of possession team lying in wait for a mistake. United clear the Fulham corner.

It has been revealed that bassey defends well in the area, but United are starting to warm to their task. Tielemans lifts a dangerous cross into the box, and Fernandes’s header deflects off Affengruber and behind for a corner.

A short corner comes to nothing, but from a second or possibly third phase Lisandro Martinez lets fly from distance with a swerving, outside of the left foot shot. Appeared destined for the corner, but Leno pushed the ball around the post. Great try from Martinez.

Recent findings suggest that united have settled on the ball now, enjoying some possession of their own in non-threatening areas. Neither team appears too interested in gambling on the high press, a degree of wariness in their approaches. That was a nice Fulham move, sweeping from right to left, but Iwobi chipped a cross into Lammens’s gloves. Tielemans then looks for the run of Rashford with a through ball, but the forward is offside. Plenty of green grass behind Fulham’s back four though.

Fulham move the ball well again, Robinson setting the ball back for Garcia to strike from just outside the box but he dragged his shot wide of the near post. Too much time and space for the forward if you are United inclined, though. Tielemans then passes the ball out of play, splitting the difference between Dalot and Mbeumo.

Promising signs for Josh King as he carries the ball from the right touchline into a dangerous central position, unchallenged by United’s midfield. The home team have monopolised the ball so far, United sitting off in a shape, perhaps waiting for an error and the chance to counter-attack.

United get the game under way at Craven Cottage.

Very difficult to predict what you are going to be served by either of these teams. Both of their seasons are on a knife edge even at the this early juncture.

It has been revealed that if Manchester United could choose a Premier League away fixture to revitalise their season, Fulham would be it. Not just because they are bottom of the league with just one point, albeit impressively earned last week away to Liverpool, but because United have not been beaten at Craven Cottage since December 2009 – although, not such a good omen for United, is the fact that Michael Carrick was in their team that day (playing at centre-back).

It has been revealed that michael Carrick dismissed as “ridiculous” any suggestion that his job as Manchester United’s head coach was at risk this early in the season. But he needs a positive result today against Fulham otherwise much of the prolonged international break will be taken up by debate as to whether he is up to it. United do not play again after today until they host stricken Tottenham Hotspur on October 10 and their start to this season has simply not been good enough. The concern for Carrick appears his inability to positively affect games when things are going against United.

Fulham starting XI: Leno, Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson, Berge, Charles, King, Bobb, Iwobi, Garcia.

Subs: Lecomte, Andersen, Palacios, Muniz, Kevin, Larsson, Manuel Angel, Sessegnon. Smith Rowe.

According to recent reports, here's how The Fulham shape up. ⚪️ pic.twitter.com/0IxS0J3ldf.

United starting XI: Lammens, Dalot, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Fernandes, Mbeumo, Cunha, Rashford.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Baleba, Lacey.

Presenting your United XI to face Fulham ✊.

According to recent reports, the script pretty much writes itself these days. A flicker of optimism and hope of a fresh start giving way to the same old frustrations, complaints and inquests, the cumulative toll of which places an ever greater strain on a club mired in mediocrity but with little reprieve from the expectations that come with bearing such an illustrious name.

Michael Carrick says Pro Ref’s apology over the derby fiasco means little to Manchester United – but warned his players they cannot allow such setbacks to derail their season.

Chief refereeing officer Howard Webb formally apologised to United after the VAR officials Matt Donohue and Blake Antrobus failed to spot Enzo Fernandez was offside before wrongly allowing Erling Haaland’s winning goal to stand in Manchester City’s 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

United were left shocked by the scale of the blunder, which came with 30 minutes of the game remaining and City already down to 10 men.

But Carrick has told his players not to become preoccupied with such injustices as they bid to overcome their poor start to the season before a crucial trip to Craven Cottage.

“It can have an impact in the moment of time, it can have a significant impact, but we can’t let it have an impact on the rest of the season,” the United manager mentioned.

Sources indicate that “That’s for us to get back to winning ways as soon as possible. Listen, one-off things can happen, at the time it was a pretty big one, we know that. I don’t think I need to go over that.

“But yeah, I’ve got faith in it [VAR], it’s the system that we work towards and that we use so the apology doesn’t mean an awful lot.”.

Carrick added: “I can appreciate and I respect it for them putting their hands up and saying we got that wrong, I think it happens - it does happen.

“But moving forward, yeah, we just have to deal with it, what’s thrown in front of us. And maybe we get one or two decisions on the back of how it balances out - percentages or law of averages or whatever that may be.

“But that was a pretty big one to take and had a huge impact on that game and that’s why it was particularly tough.”.

Michael Carrick may have had a point when he said it was “ridiculous” to question his future this early in the season, but this afternoon’s game at Fulham will shape the mood at Manchester United for the next three weeks.

A tally of four points from their first four games of the season is a disappointing start, and Brighton added to the sense of gloom in the League Cup by becoming the first side in 50 years to win from 2-0 down at Old Trafford.

With Champions League football on the agenda, that competition was at the bottom of United’s priority list but the ragged nature of the performance prompted boos around the stadium.

The no-show at Hull and defeat to 10-man City also fall into the “it’s how you lose” category of defeat, while there are widening fissures between the fanbase and the club’s hierarchy over ticketing policy and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s political interventions.

The mood has also been sour at Fulham in the first few weeks of the season. In fact, they start the game bottom of the Premier League with one point, but do have the incentive of knowing a draw would take them above Spurs.

Following reports of friction between some established players and new head coach Alvaro Arbeloa though, they produced their best performance of the season in a goalless draw at Anfield last week when they had chances to win the game.

Fulham made nine changes in the League Cup in mid-week, but still ran out 3-2 winners at West Ham. Despite the west London club being an established mid-table Premier League team for a number of seasons, and United’s vulnerable state for the past few years, Fulham have beaten their opponent’s just once in the league since December 2009.Full team news on the way shortly.

By Darren Plant | 21 Nov 2026 13:47, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 13:58.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has recalled goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez for Saturday's Premier League fixture against Leeds United.

Despite Martinez having proven his recovery from a fractured jaw for Argentina over the international break, many felt that Mike Penders would retain his place between the sticks.

Instead, Alonso has opted to hand Martinez a way back into the starting lineup in what is one of four changes from the 1-0 defeat at Sunderland.

Josh Acheampong has shaken off a minor fitness concern to take the spot of Marco Palestra at right-back.

Estevao Willian returns on the right flank, with Jordan Henderson dropping down to the substitutes' bench.

Meanwhile, Alonso has selected a frontline number nine, with Emanuel Emegha getting the nod over Pedro Neto for what is his first Premier League start.

Moises Caicedo has passed a fitness test to take his place in midfield.

As for Leeds, Daniel Farke has made just the one alteration to his Leeds XI for the game in West London.

Noah Okafor has been rewarded for his goal as a substitute versus Spurs with a place in the final third ahead of Lukas Nmecha.

Sean Longstaff will either line up in a three-player midfield or be used as one of two number 10s.

Chelsea XI: Martinez; Acheampong, Fofana, Colwill, Chavarria; Lavia, Caicedo; Estevao, Palmer, Rogers; Emegha.

Subs: Penders, Subuloye, Gusto, Palestra, Barco, Henderson, Neto, Quenda, Welbeck.

Leeds United XI: Trafford; Bogle, Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic, Gudmundsson; Ampadu, Longstaff, Tanaka; Okafor, Calvert-Lewin.

Subs: Zetterer, Bard, Rodon, Bijol, Stach, Aaronson, James, Wilson, Nmecha.

Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges

📅 25 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2106 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules.
  • Sources indicate that city face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League.
  • If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

Sources indicate that city face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

It has been revealed that the charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Sources indicate that each of those cases would have to be held individually, potentially leading to years more of litigation. Conversely, if City win their appeal, they too could take legal action against the Premier League the damage caused to their reputation.

Sources indicate that there has not yet been an official confirmation of the independent panel’s verdict from the Premier League. The Premier League declined to comment.

Sources indicate that however, several sources have told Telegraph Sport that the panel has found City guilty of all but one of the charges they faced. The one that has not been proved is stated to be one of the most serious of the 115.

Industry observers note that the damning verdict for City is a major new test of fragile UK relations with the United Arab Emirates, with whom bilateral trade was worth £25bn last year. Redacted freedom of information documents, seen by Telegraph Sport, show Abu Dhabi hosted UK government officials including Lord Stockwood, then investment minister, as recently as February. Khaldoon Al Mubarak, the City chairman and trusted adviser to the UAE president, was present at the meeting. Government notes from the meeting recorded that he “noted they are very proud of what they have achieved through their investments in Manchester”.

The Government previously caused acrimony among senior leaders in Abu Dhabi after putting forward legislation to ban foreign states from owning UK newspapers and news magazines. The intervention prompted the collapse of a takeover of The Telegraph in April 2024, which was largely funded by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the owner of City and vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

Industry observers note that the previous UK government has admitted its embassy in Abu Dhabi and the Foreign Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) in London discussed the charges levelled at City by the Premier League. However it refused to disclose the correspondence.

Industry observers note that city have steadfastly maintained they are innocent, promising “irrefutable” evidence in support of their position, and had assembled some of the most expensive lawyers in the country to argue their case. Despite the verdict, the club are understood to be confident that it will win the argument in the end. Senior figures are remarked to be calm about the latest development, as significant as it seems.

Recent findings suggest that city rebuilt their team this summer and it is understood that signings were brought in on conventional player contracts, rather than terms including clauses triggered in the event of a heavy punishment. Given the club have consistently denied breaching financial regulations, and their deals for newly introduced players to work with head coach Enzo Maresca underlines their position.

Sources indicate that on Friday, a City spokesman stated: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club have diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”.

Sources close to Pep Guardiola, the former City manager who stepped down last summer after 10 years of remarkable success at the club, including a treble triumph in 2023 and an unprecedented fourth straight league title in 2024, insist he has not been informed of any verdict.

In the days after City were first charged, Guardiola mounted a fierce defence of the club, claiming: “I am fully convinced we will be [proved] innocent.”.

The verdict vindicates the Premier League’s decision to launch an investigation after explosive allegations that City had routinely broken financial rules were first made in Der Spiegel in 2018 based on the Football Leaks documents.

Uefa previously accused City of breaches of its financial regulations and confirmed in 2020 that it was suspending the club from the Champions League for two years for “overstating” sponsorship revenue between 2012 and 2016.

City denied the Uefa charges and, after an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, the two-year ban was overturned. Cas found that a number of the claims brought by Uefa had fallen outside a five-year “time bar” and others were “not established”.

It did, however, still impose a €10m fine after ruling that City failed to cooperate with investigators. City had previously also agreed a settlement with Uefa of €20m in 2014 following an investigation into their finances.

In a recent development, legal experts agreed that the commission’s verdict is far from the end of the case. Yasin Patel, barrister at Church Court Chambers, noted: “City’s lawyers will now analyse this decision and look at the options open to them to appeal, which may include procedural impropriety, wrongful interpretation of law, and legal errors – importantly, they can guarantee an appeal.

According to recent reports, “Sanctions could include a major fine, points deduction, relegation or even all three. Factoring in whether titles and trophies should be stripped, whether other clubs have been robbed of further revenue and opportunities due to City’s wrongdoings and losses incurred, we safely say that this is only the first chapter of a long-running legal saga that will not end any time soon.”.

In a recent development, ian Hargreaves, partner with specialist disputes firm Quillon Law, said the verdict was “not the end of the story but the beginning of a fresh phase”, and added: “There is also the question of whether the panel’s decision can withstand a hard-fought appeal, and on what grounds any challenge might be brought. Much will depend on the detail of the panel’s findings and reasoning, which will inevitably be closely scrutinised by both sides.”.

Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri, who won the Ballon d’Or during his trophy-laden spell at the club, stated he believed the club were innocent.

Recent findings suggest that “For the players, it’s different than it is for journalists. I can understand all opinions, but we try to stay positive,” the Spain midfielder mentioned while on international duty.

Sources indicate that “When you see all the people who worked hard at City to achieve success, you know what we achieved can’t be taken away. It wasn’t paid for with money, but with effort and teamwork. Everything we achieved was deserved; we marked one of the great eras of English football. I believe in the club’s innocence – we already went through this in 2020.”.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister, remarked: “I think we would all need to study the independent commission’s report in some considerable detail before reaching any conclusions.”.

Zohran Kwame Mamdani, the mayor of New York, posted “114” in relation to the charges while former Manchester United players David de Gea and Rio Ferdinand both asked whether they should be due winner’s medals from past seasons.

The Premier League statement in February 2023 said that “a number of alleged breaches” had been referred to an independent commission. It then detailed each specific rule against each season in which the alleged breach took place. The precise number was not clear from the statement and led to varying reports between 115 and 130. Friday’s news suggested the figure was 115.

All the way to 2009-10, the first full season following the club’s takeover by Sheikh Mansour, who is a member of the Abu Dhabi Royal family and the vice president of the United Arab Emirates. There were charges relating to all 14 seasons until the Premier League completed their investigation during the 2022-23 campaign. In that time, City won seven Premier League titles, six League Cups, three FA Cups and the Champions League. They have since won another league title – the first club to do so four times in a row – as well as the Uefa Super Cup, the Fifa Club World Cup and the FA Cup and League Cup double last season.

They can be split into five groups. The biggest relates to the seasons from 2009-10 until 2017-18 and the requirement for clubs to provide accurate financial information and act in the utmost good faith.

The next set of rules concern the full disclosure of manager and player payments. The alleged manager breaches related to the period between 2009-10 and 2012-13, when Roberto Mancini was leading the team. The alleged breaches with respect to player payments relate to all of the seasons between 2010-11 and 2015-16.

Industry observers note that as well as providing financial detail, clubs were required to meet Uefa and Premier League rules which were designed to bring a club’s spending broadly in line with their income by placing set limits on losses. City were charged with breaches of Uefa’s licencing and financial fair play rules from 2013-14 until 2017-18, and the Premier League’s profit and sustainability rules from 2015-16 until 2017-18.

The final set of charges spanned the five seasons during which City were being investigated by the Premier League and rules that require members to cooperate in the utmost good faith by providing information and documents.

Industry observers note that A full picture will only emerge when the commission publishes its findings but we know that the Premier League investigation began in December 2018 following allegations in the German newspaper Der Spiegel based on the Football Leaks documents. These included alleged payments to former manager Mancini for consultancy work at an Abu Dhabi-based club that was separate to his regular contract at City.

Sources indicate that we also know that City were alleged to have breached rules over setting out image rights payments to players in their club contract. Der Spiegel reported that the Premier League investigation also focused on payments to under-age players, as well as whether club sponsors were paying for commercial deals themselves or a significant proportion was in fact effectively coming from owner Sheikh Mansour.

Sources indicate that city have always denied breaking any rules. In response to the Premier League statement about the alleged breaches, they remarked that they have “irrefutable evidence” to support their position and “look forward to this matter being put to rest once and for all.”.

At the start of the hearing in September 2024, Guardiola also said: “Wait for the independent panel. We believe we have not done anything wrong.”.

In a recent development, of the Football Leaks documents, City noted: “We will not be providing any comment on out-of-context materials. The attempt to damage the club’s reputation is organised and clear.”.
